Experience working closely with Paid Media, Creative, CRM, Product Marketing, and Analytics teams. Excellent negotiation, communication, and relationship-building skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience scaling influencer programs beyond 500 active creators. Experience building ambassador or affiliate communities using Slack, Discord, Facebook Groups, Circle, or similar platforms. Experience activating creator content through paid social advertising. Experience leveraging AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, or equivalent platforms to improve recruiting, reporting, communication, and workflow efficiency. jobs.title: Senior Growth Marketing Manager
jobs.description: About BiOptimizers BiOptimizers exist to help people go from baseline health to peak biological performance. We develop science-backed supplements and wellness tools that deliver measurable results. As a remote-first company, our globally distributed team focuses on clarity, autonomy, and operational excellence. Every role is designed to support the health and performance of both our customers and our organization. Role Overview We’re hiring a Senior Growth Marketing Manager to scale our direct-to-consumer (DTC) business by acquiring new customers — and specifically new subscribers — profitably, at or below our target customer acquisition cost (CAC). This is the core of the role: bring in high-quality subscribers at a CAC that works against their lifetime value, and then scale that engine without breaking the economics. This is a hands-on, in-the-platform operator role — not a strategy-only seat. You will build, launch, and optimize paid campaigns daily across Meta and Google, extend into video and TV as we scale, and own the full path from ad impression to subscribed customer — including the offers, the creative, and the landing pages that convert a first-time visitor into a recurring subscriber. You understand that new-customer CAC — not blended ROAS — is the number that matters, and that acquiring a subscriber is worth more than a one-time buyer because subscriber retention and LTV set how much you can profitably spend to acquire. You keep ad message, audience signal, offer, and landing page tightly aligned to drive subscription take-rate. This role reports into marketing leadership and contributes directly to BiOptimizers’ mission of biologically optimizing the health of humanity. Key Responsibilities New-subscriber acquisition at or below target CAC — you own the number, the spend, and the outcome. Daily, hands-on management of paid acquisition across Meta and Google, scaling profitable spend as fast as the CAC target allows. The acquisition offer and funnel — how first-order offers, subscribe-and-save mechanics, and checkout drive subscription take-rate, first-order margin, and payback. The creative and landing-page system that converts cold traffic into subscribers, in partnership with creative and front-end development. A repeatable creator-content testing pipeline that graduates winning organic concepts into paid ads. Expansion into upper-funnel video and TV (linear / CTV) as the account scales, measured for true incrementality. Required Qualifications 7+ years of hands-on, in-platform paid acquisition experience for a DTC or consumer brand — you have personally managed budgets and owned CAC and performance, not just briefed an agency. A proven track record of acquiring new customers profitably at a target CAC and scaling spend without blowing up the economics. Subscription / recurring-revenue acquisition experience is strongly preferred — you understand how subscriber retention and LTV set your allowable CAC and payback window, and how offers and checkout drive subscription take-rate. Deep, hands-on Meta Ads management: campaign structure, Advantage+ Shopping and broad targeting, creative testing, and budget scaling. You understand Meta’s Andromeda retrieval engine and how creative volume, signal quality (CAPI / server-side), and audience consolidation feed it to improve delivery and lower CAC. Hands-on Google Ads management across Search, Performance Max, and YouTube — including asset group construction, search-term mining, brand vs. non-brand separation, and negative keyword discipline. Working knowledge of how to buy linear TV and/or connected TV (CTV), including how upper-funnel video is planned, trafficked, and measured for incrementality alongside lower-funnel paid social and search. Strong command of how landing pages interact with ads — message match between ad and page, page speed and structure, and how landing page experience drives (or kills) conversion rate and downstream ad performance. You can spec, test, and iterate on pages, not just hand them off. A working understanding of full-funnel creative and how it maps to intent: top-of-funnel content that stops the scroll and earns attention, middle-of-funnel that builds belief and educates, and bottom-of-funnel that converts. You know how hooks, offers, and calls-to-action change by funnel stage and can direct or brief creative accordingly. Working knowledge of TikTok as a growth channel, and — critically — how to build a repeatable system for testing content with creators: sourcing and briefing creators, running organic content as a testing ground, reading what resonates, and graduating winning concepts into paid ads across TikTok and Meta. Fluency in data-driven decision-making and A/B testing — you design clean tests, read results correctly, and act on them. Comfortable with Google Analytics and attribution platforms. Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience. Preferred Qualifications Experience scaling subscriber acquisition for a consumer wellness or supplement brand in a hypergrowth environment. Hands-on experience with subscription platforms (e.g., Recharge) and optimizing subscribe-and-save offers and churn. Experience designing and reading geo holdout or incrementality tests, especially for video / TV spend. Familiarity with omnichannel dynamics — how DTC, Amazon, and retail interact, including the effect of branded-search and pricing across channels. Work Location This is a fully remote position. jobs.description: Flashpoint is the pioneering leader in threat data and intelligence. We empower commercial enterprises and government agencies to decisively confront complex security challenges, reduce risk, and improve operational resilience amid fast-evolving threats. Through the Flashpoint Ignite platform, we deliver unparalleled depth, breadth and speed of data from highly relevant sources, enriched by human insights. Our solutions span cyber threat intelligence, vulnerability intelligence, geopolitical risk, physical security, fraud and brand protection. The result: our customers safeguard critical assets, avoid financial loss, and protect lives. Discover more at flashpoint.io Are you an experienced product marketer who thrives at the intersection of positioning, storytelling, and go-to-market strategy? Flashpoint is looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager to join our Product Marketing team, remote in the United States. In this role, you will own the go-to-market strategy for our core cyber threat intelligence offerings, shaping our value proposition, positioning, messaging, and competitive differentiation, and evolving pricing and packaging as we scale. You will sit at the intersection of Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Marketing, working closely with your manager to translate technical capability into a narrative that resonates with CISOs and security practitioners around the world. This is a high-visibility seat: your work directly shapes our market position, win rates, deal value, and company growth. We have a role for you if, you: Build and run product marketing programs for SaaS B2B threat intelligence or cybersecurity software. Own product launches end to end, from positioning through sales enablement to measurable adoption. Translate complex technical capability into messaging and assets that sales teams actively use in the field. Drive cross-functional GTM initiatives across Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Marketing to measurable results. Have briefed executives, boards, or industry analysts on competitive and market dynamics. Shape pricing and packaging strategy for SaaS products. Are genuinely curious about applying AI to product marketing work, and have put it to work within your roles. What you will get to do on our team: Create differentiated positioning and messaging grounded in a clear understanding of the buyer, the market, and Flashpoint's core capabilities. Drive awareness, pipeline, and growth for Flashpoint's threat intelligence offerings. Own the product marketing strategy and roadmap for key offerings. Partner cross-functionally to design and execute GTM initiatives and commercialization efforts that drive measurable results. Build sales and marketing content, including collateral, thought leadership, solution presentations, and website content, that moves buyers through the funnel. Equip sales and partner teams with the messaging, training, and support structures they need to run a strong sales motion. Become the resident expert on target buyers, market trends, and the competitive landscape, and use that expertise to shape planning. Represent Flashpoint as a thought leader through publishing, social, and webinars. What you will achieve: Within 30 days You will learn Flashpoint's vision, mission, strategy, and culture, and meet with your manager and key stakeholders across leadership, marketing, product, intelligence, sales, and customer success. You will get up to speed on Flashpoint's product and service offerings and the competitive landscape. You will analyze customer engagements and feedback to understand the business outcomes Flashpoint drives for them, and review prospect data to identify the biggest levers and blockers in the sales cycle. Within 60 days You will contribute to a GTM initiative aimed at new business or existing-customer upsell. You will complete a content audit and map content to the buyer's journey to drive conversion. You will have built working competitive intelligence resources for your product area, and articulated how Flashpoint differentiates itself. By 90 days You will have a prioritized action plan for your area of the PMM team, aligned to Flashpoint's corporate and marketing goals. You will have built a product demo and delivered a training session to Sales so they can confidently communicate the value of our solutions to prospects and customers. You will translate the product roadmap for your area into a unified launch strategy that supports the broader business. To be successful in this role, you will need: Product marketing experience in cybersecurity or threat intelligence software. Strong written and presentation skills you can point to, such as decks, launches, or competitive briefs. Experience shaping pricing and packaging strategy for a SaaS product. The ability to run multiple concurrent initiatives without losing momentum. Base Pay Range: $150,000-165,000/yr plus target bonus Why Flashpoint is a Great Place to Work: Diversity . That’s why we also prioritize health and wellness perks like gym reimbursements, expensed lunches, cool cultural initiatives and inclusive employee events. Career Growth. We encourage regular one-on-ones with your manager, a regular schedule of performance reviews, learning and development opportunities, and guidance through formalized career paths; whether that be towards being a great manager, being a great individual contributor, or a lateral move to gain breadth of knowledge and experience. By doing so, you'll stay updated with Flashpoint news and upcoming career opportunities. Even if you're not ready to apply now, being part of our Talent Network ensures you won't miss out on exciting opportunities in the future.

jobs.title: Lifecycle Marketing Lead (Remote US)
jobs.description: Directive Consulting is the leading B2B performance marketing agency that delivers real revenue—not just leads. We use Customer Generation (a marketing methodology developed by us) to cut through the noise. Forget MQLs—we’re here to drive pipeline, fuel SQLs, and scale brands that are serious about growth. From Paid Media and SEO to CRO, RevOps, and Go-To-Market Strategy, we build marketing engines that win in SaaS and across B2B industries. We move fast. We think boldly. We are elite. We hire people who challenge the status quo and push campaigns past what’s expected - sparking demand for bold, innovative brands. If you live for performance, love solving hard problems, and want your work to actually mean something , you’ll fit right in. But here’s the fun part—we don’t just deliver results; we’re shaping the future of marketing. Ready to build something that breaks the mold? The Role Directive is building a dedicated Lifecycle Marketing practice designed to help clients turn more of the demand they already generate into pipeline, revenue, repeat purchases, expansion, and long-term customer value. We are looking for an Associate Director of Lifecycle Marketing to help build that offering from the ground up. This is a player-coach role from day one . You will be hands-on with strategy, platform architecture, client delivery, and execution while also helping define how Directive approaches Lifecycle Marketing as a practice. As the offering grows, you will help hire, mentor, and develop the team around you while continuing to stay close to our most strategic and complex client work. You will have significant autonomy to shape the practice, including our methodology, service offerings, delivery model, technology recommendations, measurement frameworks, and how we bring Lifecycle Marketing to market. You will work closely with the Director and Managing Director, who will provide strategic direction, support, and partnership while giving you room to build. This is not a role for someone looking to inherit a finished playbook. We have a strong starting point, but we are looking for someone with the experience and point of view to challenge it, improve it, and help us create something meaningfully differentiated. The Clients You'll Support Our Lifecycle Marketing practice supports two fundamentally different revenue models. You need to be able to operate across both and teach others how to do the same. eCommerce Direct Commerce Retention: Distributors, manufacturers, and other businesses with a direct purchasing relationship and trackable order history. Channel & Partner Enablement Lifecycle: Manufacturers selling through distributors, dealers, resellers, or other channel partners. In these environments, the lifecycle audience may be the channel partner rather than the end buyer. Service & SaaS Lead Nurture & Pipeline Acceleration: Our Service and SaaS clients generate handraisers across paid media, organic, events, content, and other acquisition channels. Lifecycle Marketing helps turn those handraisers into qualified opportunities and customers in partnership with the client's sales and BDR teams. Customer Expansion & Subscription Growth: Once a prospect becomes a customer, Lifecycle Marketing can help deepen that relationship. What You'll Do Lifecycle Strategy & Architecture: You will help establish how Directive approaches Lifecycle Marketing across both eCommerce and Service/SaaS clients. Build lifecycle strategies rooted in the client's revenue model, customer journey, data, and business objectives. Architect end-to-end customer and prospect journeys across acquisition, nurture, conversion, onboarding, retention, expansion, and re-engagement. Develop segmentation strategies using demographic, firmographic, behavioral, purchase, engagement, lifecycle-stage, and account data. Identify gaps in existing lifecycle programs and prioritize the highest-impact opportunities. Build testing roadmaps across messaging, timing, audience, journey structure, offers, and conversion points. Establish measurement frameworks that connect lifecycle activity to meaningful business outcomes. Hands-On Client Delivery You will be expected to build alongside the team and act not only as a strategy-only leader. Platforms & Technology You will work across client technology stacks rather than operating within a single platform. Client Leadership As a senior member of the practice, you will own relationships, not simply deliver assigned tasks. Build the Lifecycle Marketing Practice A meaningful part of this role is building the offering itself. You will have the autonomy to influence as you begin with shared early-stage frameworks, not rigid rules. We expect you to finish what is incomplete, improve what can be better, and introduce new approaches when your experience tells you there is a stronger way to solve the problem. Sales, Scoping & Growth As a foundational leader of the offering, you will also help Directive determine where Lifecycle Marketing can create value before an engagement begins. Over time, you will become one of the people Directive's Sales and Client teams turn to when they need to understand what a strong Lifecycle Marketing engagement should look like. What We're Looking For Player-Coach Leadership. Initially, time will be spent building and directly delivering client work. As revenue and headcount grow, responsibilities will increasingly include developing the people around you. 6+ years of experience across Lifecycle Marketing, CRM, marketing automation, retention, or related disciplines. Meaningful experience supporting B2B, SaaS, Service, or complex eCommerce business models . A purely traditional DTC background is unlikely to be enough for this role. Hands-on experience architecting lifecycle programs from scratch rather than only optimizing established programs. Strong understanding of segmentation, automation, customer journeys, trigger logic, experimentation, and lifecycle measurement. Working expertise in at least two major lifecycle or marketing automation platforms such as HubSpot, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Pardot, Klaviyo, Marketo, or Attentive. Experience working with imperfect data and creating practical strategies despite technical limitations. Strong client-facing communication and the ability to confidently lead conversations with senior stakeholders. Experience connecting lifecycle activity to pipeline, revenue, retention, expansion, or other meaningful business outcomes. Previous experience mentoring, managing, or informally developing other marketers. Ability to move between strategy and execution without seeing hands-on work as "below" the role. Strong commercial instincts and comfort participating in scoping, pitching, or expanding client engagements. Comfort operating in ambiguity and creating structure where little exists today. A strong point of view paired with a willingness to change that point of view when the data or client context calls for it. Strong Plus Agency or consulting experience managing multiple clients simultaneously. Experience supporting both eCommerce and B2B/SaaS lifecycle programs. Experience with manufacturer, distributor, dealer, reseller, or other channel-driven revenue models. Experience with ERP environments such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Epicor, or Infor and their relationship to customer and marketing data. Experience with SMS strategy, technology evaluation, implementation, and optimization. Experience partnering closely with RevOps, Sales Operations, or Marketing Operations teams. Experience auditing lifecycle programs and translating findings into paid consulting engagements. Previous responsibility for scoping, pitching, or selling professional services. Experience helping build a new capability, department, or service offering. Platform certifications across HubSpot, Salesforce, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Klaviyo, or comparable technologies. This is a true player-coach role. Your PMMs own their product portfolios, and you'll guide their strategy and raise the quality of their work while directly owning company-level and cross-portfolio initiatives yourself. It's hands-on by design: you get the scope and influence of a senior leader while staying close to the craft. AI fluency is table stakes for this role. We expect AI to be foundational to how you analyze information, build workflows, create and evaluate work, and scale the team's impact without compromising quality. Key responsibilities Positioning and market strategy Own Procurify's positioning strategy and define how we differentiate in the procurement market. Build and maintain the company-level narrative and messaging architecture as the single source of truth across all surfaces, and translate it into positioning teams can execute against. Own the AI and agentic narrative: make the platform's intelligence concrete, credible, and differentiated for finance and operations buyers. Own market segmentation and use it to direct where we invest and who we talk to. Own the voice of the customer with deep customer research and win/loss analysis. Own the strategy for direct-to-customer communications: launch and product-news emails, in-app posts, in-app tours, and lifecycle journeys. Establish shared tools, context, and repeatable workflows across core PMM work, and partner with Marketing’s AI specialists to make Product Marketing a model for effective AI-assisted work. Own the enablement deliverable set for each product portfolio with your PMMs, including positioning one-pagers, battlecards, playbooks, demo narratives, and objection handling, maintained as living resources in our library rather than launch-day artifacts. Train Sales and Customer Success on messaging, use cases, and differentiation. Set the standard for how competitive intelligence gets gathered and used by go-to-market teams. And we're looking for someone who wants to help us open a LOT more of them. So... What Does Your Day Actually Look Like? 8:30 AM: You open your laptop. Coffee? Obviously. You check yesterday's numbers and notice that applications from one of our newest states are up 18%. Great. Then you notice conversion on one of the highest-traffic pages dropped 7%. Less great. You start digging. 9:15 AM: You're in a launch meeting for a new state. Paid media wants creative. Content has questions about state-specific messaging. Partnerships thinks there might be a compliance wrinkle. Someone asks, "Are we still on track for launch?" You smile. Yes. You are. Because you already built the launch plan, assigned owners, set deadlines, and have approximately 47 tabs open keeping everything moving. You are the quarterback. 10:30 AM: Time to get into the weeds. You’re reviewing SEO performance and thinking about: Which keywords actually drive enrollment—not just traffic Which program and state pages need attention Technical SEO issues Structured data and schema Metadata and heading structure Internal linking URL architecture How pages are showing up in search and increasingly, AI-generated answers You don't need to be the person writing every line of code. But you do need to know enough to say, "That's going to hurt indexation," before it becomes a problem. 11:30 AM: You find a landing page with a 4.2% conversion rate. Your reaction: "We can do better." So you pull the funnel data. You look at traffic sources. You look at drop-off points. You formulate a hypothesis. You build an A/B test. Maybe the headline needs work. Maybe the CTA is buried. Maybe the page is asking families to do too much too soon. You don't spend three weeks debating it. You test it. Because at OpenEd, we'd rather learn from an experiment than admire a PowerPoint about one. 12:30 PM: Lunch. Probably while checking Slack. We won't judge. 1:00 PM: Lifecycle marketing time. You’re building and optimizing the journeys that turn: "I'm curious about OpenEd" → "Tell me more" → "I'm interested" → "I'm applying" → "We're enrolled." You’re working on nurture campaigns, re-engagement, TOFU/MOFU flows, segmentation, automation, and referral mechanics. Because happy families aren't just the end of the funnel. They can be the beginning of the next one. 2:00 PM: Your paid media agency sends the monthly performance report. You open it. You have questions. Lots of questions. You’re looking at paid search, paid social, creative, audiences, cost efficiency, qualified leads, and—most importantly—whether all that spending is actually helping more families enroll. You're not managing the agency so you can forward reports around. You're managing them because you own the outcome. 3:00 PM: Someone asks: "How's the new state launch going?" You don't answer, "Pretty well!" You have the numbers. Traffic. Conversion by page. Conversion by source. Applications. Lead-to-enrollment rates. Referral activity. Spend efficiency. You know what's working. You know what's not. And you already have a recommendation for what to do next. 4:00 PM: Surprise! Something changed. A campaign isn't performing. A launch timeline moved. A landing page needs to ship. A partner has a new opportunity. Someone needs a decision. You reprioritize. You make the hard call. You keep moving. Because "we should probably..." isn't really your favorite phrase. "I did." is. 5:00 PM: You look at your launch calendar. Another state is coming. You tweak the playbook based on what you learned today. Because the goal isn't to launch one market successfully. It's to build a repeatable growth engine that makes every launch faster, smarter, and more efficient than the last. And then you shut your laptop. Tomorrow, you'll do it again. Probably with more coffee. What You'll Own: 🚀 New State Launches You'll quarterback new state launches from end to end, bringing together paid, SEO, lifecycle, content, brand, and partnerships into one coordinated GTM strategy. You'll continuously improve the launch playbook and incorporate state-specific regulatory and market considerations into acquisition strategy. 🔎 SEO Strategy You'll own SEO strategy and keyword priorities for the pages that actually drive enrollment. You'll guide technical SEO recommendations across program and state pages, including schema, metadata, heading structure, internal linking, URL structure, and on-page conventions. You'll also help shape page templates and layouts so our programs can be found—not just by Google, but by the increasingly important world of AI-powered search. 🧪 Website Conversion & CRO You'll own conversion strategy for our highest-impact program pages. You'll analyze funnels, run A/B tests, experiment with landing pages, and partner with the team to ship experiences that turn more visitors into applicants. 💌 Lifecycle & Email You'll own lifecycle marketing across nurture, re-engagement, TOFU, MOFU, and referral journeys. You'll build segmented, automated experiences that help move families from first interaction to enrollment—and turn happy families into advocates. 🗣️ Word of Mouth & Referral Some of our strongest growth comes from families telling other families. Co-ops, Facebook groups, neighbors, the mom at the park. It's one of our most important channels, and we don't want it to be an accident. You'll own making it deliberate: building referral mechanics into lifecycle flows, working alongside our ambassador program. It already works. Your job is to make it compound. 💰 Paid Acquisition & Agency Management You'll manage our paid media agency, establish growth targets, review performance, and push for better results. You'll continuously test creative, audiences, and channels to increase awareness, qualified applications, and enrollment while improving efficiency. 📊 Analytics & Reporting You'll own state-level pipeline reporting and turn data into decisions. You'll track traffic, conversion by page and source, lead-to-enrollment rates, paid performance, word-of-mouth, referrals, and other acquisition sources. In other words: You won't just report what happened. You'll tell us what we should do about it. How We'll Know You're Winning You'll help us: Grow awareness and reach in target markets Generate more qualified applications Successfully launch new states Improve website and funnel conversion Increase lead-to-enrollment conversion Improve marketing efficiency as markets mature Build repeatable systems that make every launch better than the last Who Are You? You're someone who: Has 5+ years of B2C/DTC growth or performance marketing experience acquiring consumers at scale (with B2C experience within the last 5 years) Has managed multiple markets, regions, or campaigns simultaneously Knows paid search and paid social and has a track record of generating qualified leads Has managed agencies or external partners against performance goals Understands SEO strategy and technical SEO fundamentals Has hands-on CRO, A/B testing, and landing-page experience Has built lifecycle and email programs using marketing automation tools Loves analytics and knows how to turn numbers into action Has Webflow experience (strongly preferred) Is ridiculously organized—you set dates, own deadlines, and actually hit them Can juggle multiple channels, campaigns, and launches without losing your mind Is comfortable working independently and figuring things out This Role Will Make You Very Happy If... You are a builder. You don't want to spend your day managing someone else's strategy. You want to build the landing page. Launch the campaign. Write the brief. Pull the data. Spot the problem. Run the test. Fix the funnel. And see what happens. You like having an opinion—and you're perfectly comfortable changing it when the data proves you wrong. You care deeply about helping families access better educational options. You like moving fast without sacrificing quality. And the idea of owning growth across an expanding portfolio of states sounds less like "a lot of work" and more like: "Where do I sign?" Our Culture: High Standards. Low Ego. Culture at OpenEd is intentional. It's defined by what we promote—and what we tolerate. Our latest eNPS of 77 places OpenEd in the top 0.1% of technology companies. We don't put values on a wall and forget about them. We actually use them. Customer First Be obsessed with creating value for learners and families. Hard Choices, Easy Life Address difficult things directly, quickly, and transparently. I Did > We Should Ideas are great. Execution is better. Learn Out Loud Share what you're learning. Give feedback. Leave your ego at the door. Prioritize Ruthlessly Do a few important things exceptionally well. Fast AND World Class Move quickly. Don't lower the bar. Strong Opinions, Weakly Held Make the case. Listen. Change your mind when the evidence says you should. Make Others Famous Make the people around you better—and make sure they get the credit. The Team & Your Autonomy: You'll join a team of five. That's it. Five people covering growth, content, paid, lifecycle, referral, and the ambassador program across a 13-state footprint. A lean, mean marketing machine. Which means two things. First, you'll have real ownership from day one. There's no layer between you and the work. Second, you'll never be doing it alone. This is a team that genuinely collaborates. We share what's working, steal each other's good ideas, and make each other better. (See: Make Others Famous. ) You'll work closely with the Director, Growth Marketing on strategy and priorities, but this is not a "wait for permission" kind of role. You'll have significant day-to-day autonomy to experiment, iterate, and ship based on data. You'll personally stand up pages, campaigns, lifecycle flows, and launch programs while managing external agencies where they can extend your reach. You own execution across a growing portfolio of states. Translation: If you see something that needs to happen, we're looking for someone who makes it happen. What We Offer: Competitive salary 401(k) with company matching opportunities Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, critical illness, accident, STD/LTD, HSA, and FSA benefits Fully remote work environment Flexible working hours with an emphasis on healthy work-life balance Generous PTO A collaborative, supportive team where your work actually matters Ready to Open More Doors? If you're a hands-on growth marketer who loves data, moves quickly, builds things, asks "why?", and gets a little too excited about improving conversion rates... We should talk. There are a lot more families out there looking for a better way to educate their children. Let's help them find it. EEO Statement OpenEd is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Brand Marketing Manager
jobs.description: About Tin Can Tin Can is building a safer, simpler way for kids to connect — without smartphones. We’re creating screen-free, delightful devices and services that let families call the people who matter most, free from the noise of today’s digital world. We’re building a bold, authentic, nostalgic, and kinda quirky brand that resonates with folks who want something simpler & better for their kids than the tech-infused lives we’re currently living (and who have a sense of humor about it). As we gear up to scale to thousands of families, we’re ready to bring on a Brand Marketing Manager to help make it happen. The Role We're looking for a Brand Marketing Manager who's just as happy staring at a blank whiteboard dreaming up something delightful as they are staring at a Gantt chart making sure that idea actually happens. You'll report to our Head of Brand Strategy & Communications and work closely and collaboratively with teams across the company. This isn't a "take the brief and go" role. We want someone with real creative judgment, someone who gets Tin Can, relishes the weird and wonderful challenge we're up against, and feels how lucky we are to be handing kids the chance to build real, meaningful connections. You'll help us decide who we team up with, how we bring product moments to life (online and IRL), and how we keep parents and kids engaged in unexpected ways. You're a big thinker and a doer in equal measure. Building the workback plan delights you almost as much as pitching the idea that needed one. You write clearly, you communicate constantly, and you know an idea is only as good as its execution. If you keep a mental file of what iconic, boundary-pushing brands do right, get energy from doing five different things before 11am, don't need hand-holding, and take real pride in the follow-through — we should definitely get on the phone. What You'll Do Partnerships & collaborations. Bring us the unexpected, brand-true partnership ideas we haven't thought of yet, and go build relationships with the people and companies who share our values. You know what's right for Tin Can on instinct, and you move on it. Project management & campaign coordination. Keep every brand initiative on track across a dozen moving pieces — timelines, stakeholders, the works — so things get from brief to launch without a single dropped ball. You're the glue between creative and strategy, and you help us hit aggressive deadlines with gusto! Campaign briefs. Turn our best ideas into briefs that lay out the why, how, and what clearly enough that creative work has a strategic foundation before it ever hits production. Brand influencers. Manage our top-tier celebrity and influencer relationships and turn our most high-profile customers into our loudest advocates. Find new, authentic ways to pull them into our world. Brand stewardship. You are the Tin Can brand out in the world — newsletter, partner decks, campaign assets, all of it — making sure the experience feels like us whether it's someone's first touchpoint or their one-hundred-and-sixty-seventh. Reporting & tracking. Own the post-campaign wrap-up across your world; what worked, what didn't, and why, so we're always getting sharper. What We're Looking For 4–6 years of marketing experience, ideally at a consumer brand, DTC startup, or agency with consumer clients. You've had your hands in enough of the marketing mix to know what good looks like, and you're always thinking up new ways to do it well. Strong writing and verbal skills. Everything from a cold outreach email to a campaign brief sounds like it came from the same brand. You’re not necessarily a copywriter but you’re not not good at copywriting. A creative point of view. You get us, and you have real opinions on how we show up in the world. You know what's cool, and you never forget we're talking to two audiences at once: parents and kids. Brand, brand, brand. You get why it matters more than almost anything else here, and you take real ownership over how we evolve and grow it. Comfort with celebrity and partnership work. You've navigated brand-partner relationships before and know how to keep a conversation moving. Even better: you already have a running list of ideas for our growing roster of famous Tin Can households. Serious project management instincts. You build the tracker, set the deadline, and chase people down without being asked twice. A collaborative, low-ego approach. You'll be in and out of every function constantly — trust is as much a part of the job as taste is. An ownership mindset. Helping build Tin Can's brand marketing function from here is genuinely exciting to you. Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward action. The playbook's still being written. We need someone who sees that as the fun part. If the idea of shaping the Tin Can brand at a genuinely pivotal moment gives you butterflies, we want to hear from you!

jobs.description: About Tin Can Here at Tin Can, we're working to give kids the social independence we had growing up—without smartphones. Creative : If the current pipeline can't keep pace with what paid needs, you have the standing to ask for more—and get it. Why Join Tin Can? We're building tech that protects childhood. We're on a quest to give kids a more analog childhood—one with real conversations, real connection, and way less screen time. This is a rare chance to build something that truly matters. A seat with real reach. Paid is how most families meet us for the first time. You own that first impression and the growth that follows—not one narrow slice of it. Small, high-trust team. Every company says "team," but at Tin Can it means something different. We're a small, mission-driven group that genuinely has each other's backs—professionally and personally. Your ideas and instincts matter from day one. If you're ready to build the engine that introduces Tin Can to the next hundred thousand families, we'd love to hear from you. Reach out with your resume and a short note on the paid program you're proudest of—what you inherited, what you changed, and what it looks like now.

jobs.description: Build a Safer World. TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure. TRM Labs is building the global standard for investigations. We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager who understands that this role is not content production. It's market ownership. Your job is to make TRM the obvious choice for a specific set of buyers. You work closely with a Product Manager and Sales — the PM builds, Sales opens doors, and you make sure buyers arrive already convinced. AI handles the execution. You handle the judgment. Product marketers at TRM make the category feel like TRM's home turf before a buyer ever talks to anyone. What you'll own You'll own the market position for TRM's AI-native investigation platform. Your buyers are investigators and analysts running complex, high-stakes cases where the quality of their tooling directly determines outcomes. Your job is to make TRM the platform they can't imagine working without. That means deep fluency with how government investigations actually run, positioning that speaks to the specific workflow pressures these buyers face, and ownership of the moments where TRM cements its position as the standard. How you'll work Deep diving: You know the product at the level where you can demo it as well as anyone in the company. You know where the real value sits and where it breaks down. You're in deal reviews and customer conversations often enough to know what lands, and you can hold a real conversation with both engineering and buyers. Positioning: You find the wedge: the framing where a prospect chooses TRM every time and asking about the competition sounds like the wrong question. You build the architecture everything hangs from: the claims, the proof, the hierarchy, the words TRM owns. Tight enough that a new hire and a ten-year veteran say the same true thing. Incepting: The story only works if the company believes it first. You get Sales carrying the message without you in the room, engineers who can explain why what they're building matters, and execs who open deals with the same frame you set. You don't mandate alignment. You create it by making the story so clear and compelling that people want to tell it. Owning the moment: A tier-one launch, a CEO keynote, the webpage a buyer lands on before they ever take a meeting. These are the moments where TRM either makes an impression or misses one. You own the narrative, the timing, and the outcome. The bar is a defining moment the whole company points to. You don't wait for those. You go make them. What we're looking for Storytelling. You think in narrative, not slides. You can make something technical matter to a stranger in two sentences. Your stories are grounded in data: win/loss patterns, customer signals, market evidence, because the most persuasive narrative is one that's actually true. You translate the same story across a keynote, a one-pager, and a website without losing what makes it land. Commercial instincts. You understand what moves a deal, not just what sounds good in a deck. You've been present enough in the sales cycle to know the difference, and you've changed your positioning because of it. AI builder. You build systems for the team, not just yourself. You've already offloaded the repeatable work to automation: competitive monitoring, content generation, persona synthesis. You spend your time on the judgment calls that actually require you. Walk us through something you built that made the whole team faster. Judgment. You know what good looks like across the work and you say so when it isn't: a positioning brief that almost works, a website that doesn't land, a design that misses. You hold the standard and give feedback that moves things forward, not feedback that leaves people guessing. Hard requirements 5+ years in product marketing at a B2B SaaS company You've owned at least two tier-one launches end to end: strategy, narrative, execution, and post-launch measurement You've owned a website or major digital channel and made content decisions that moved pipeline, not just pageviews You already use AI to build workflows and systems and can walk through a real example of something you built for your team, not just yourself Deal breakers Marketers who measure output in assets shipped Anyone who treats AI as something to explore rather than something already running in their workflow Candidates whose best examples inherited existing infrastructure. We need builders, not operators of programs someone else built. About the team TRM's product team doesn't coordinate work. It owns outcomes. Product marketers are embedded in the sales motion, in customer conversations, and in launch decisions. The team is small, the scope is real, and what you ship shows up directly in how deals close and how the market talks about TRM. PMMs here don't wait to be asked. If the standard is slipping somewhere, you say so and help. AI is how we work, not just what we build. What TRM speed looks like in this role Build an agent that scans the market for opportunities and builds a prototype for new product features that the product management team reviews Customer needs a product brochure before a meeting. You build something on-brand with the right content and get it to them today, without spinning up a design cycle. Fast and accurate does more for the deal than slow and polished. Hear the CEO's keynote brief in the morning. Share core message and outline by that afternoon. jobs.title: Senior Sales Marketing Manager
jobs.description: Channel Factory provides intelligent marketing solutions for the next generation of contextual safety, suitability, and performance for brands and agencies. Our platform helps marketers implement, automate, and scale their video advertising programs across YouTube, Social Platforms and CTV. We sit at the intersection of suitability, context, and performance with a mission of enabling the world’s top brands to consciously connect with the right audience in the right context. Channel Factory embodies a strong start-up culture that values diversity, collaboration, and results. Our bias toward execution balances critical thinking, analysis, and pragmatic problem-solving. We expect a lot from one another and value our thoughtful, intellectually curious company culture. Remote work status is subject to change at any time. Channel Factory is headquartered in the United States with global offices across 40+ cities and countries. This position will be based in New York. We are seeking an exceptional, narrative-driven Sr. Manager, Sales Marketing to lead the strategic storytelling, deck architecture, and go-to-market solution packaging across our commercial organization. This role sits at the critical intersection of high-level strategy and high-craft visual storytelling. You will be responsible for translating complex adtech capabilities—spanning AI-driven contextual intelligence, multi-platform walled garden activation, dynamic creative optimization, and proprietary suitability data—into punchy, compelling sales narratives and standardized media solutions. The ideal candidate comes from a high-velocity adtech or digital media background where winning business requires market hustle, strategic differentiation, and the ability to craft category-defining presentations that captivate agency holding companies and enterprise brand marketers. Key Responsibilities 1. Elite Presentation Crafting & Strategic Narrative Design Master Storytelling & Deck Architecture: Architect and design high-impact pitch decks, keynotes, and RFP responses with flawless visual flow, executive clarity, and compelling storytelling. Complexity to Simplicity: Distill technical adtech products into clear, differentiated commercial propositions that arm sellers to win. Visual Standards: Elevate the standard of visual communication across the sales organization, creating presentation templates that balance clean aesthetic rigor with persuasive narrative arcs. 2. Strategic Media Solutions & GTM Packaging Verticalized Solutions: Proactively package Channel Factory’s platform capabilities into repeatable, high-margin vertical solutions (e.g., QSR, Auto, CPG, Retail, Entertainment) and seasonal tent-pole opportunities. Proactive Commercial Strategy: Shift sales marketing from reactive pitch support to proactive market-making by building standardized packages that can be cross-sold across holding company portfolios and independent mid-tier agencies. Case Studies & Proof Points: Transform campaign performance data and post-campaign wraps into powerful proof-point narratives that demonstrate business impact and drive client retention. 3. Sales Enablement & High-Stakes Client Programs Strategic Client Programs: Partner directly with sales leadership and brand partnership teams to co-create bespoke collateral for large-scale enterprise proposals, joint business plans (JBPs), and agency upfronts. Roadshow & Agency Content: Develop content and talk tracks for lunch & learn sessions, executive roadshows, and marketplace education forums. Seller Toolkits: Build and maintain an intuitive repository of one-sheeters, objection-handling guides, competitive battle-cards, and collateral infused with fresh industry insights. 4. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Market Intelligence Product & Marketing Bridge: Collaborate closely with Product Marketing, Research, and Regional Marketing teams (US, EMEA, APAC, LATAM) to maintain global narrative alignment while adapting materials for local market realities. Market Feedback Loop: Gather real-time intelligence from client meetings and the competitive landscape to inform ongoing positioning, research reports, and GTM priorities. 5. Additional Responsibilities Additional responsibilities and duties as assigned. Requirements To be considered for this role, candidates must meet the following criteria: 5-7 years of experience in sales marketing, product marketing, or commercial strategy within the adtech, programmatic, digital media, or agency ecosystem. World-Class Presentation & Storytelling Portfolio: A proven track record of creating visually stunning, narrative-driven sales decks, keynotes, and client collateral (a portfolio of sample presentations will be requested). Deep AdTech & Media Domain Expertise: Robust understanding of video advertising, programmatic buying, CTV/OTT, social walled gardens (YouTube, Meta, TikTok), contextual targeting, and brand safety/suitability. Strategic Packaging Acumen: Demonstrated ability to turn complex tech capabilities and disjointed data points into structured, commercially viable media packages. High-Velocity Execution: Self-starter mindset capable of managing multiple high-priority deliverables simultaneously in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. Executive Presence: Strong interpersonal skills to collaborate directly with C-level executives, sales leads, and major agency partners. Hybrid: minimum of 3 days in office. Travel: Occasional travel for key client presentations, agency roadshows, team summits, and industry events. Preferred Qualifications Experience working inside aggressive, high-growth adtech environments where value-based selling and narrative differentiation are paramount. Proficiency with modern presentation design tools (Google Slides, PowerPoint, Keynote, Figma) and familiarity with leveraging AI-assisted workflow tools to accelerate collateral production. Prior experience packaging solutions specifically for key verticals such as Quick Service Restaurants (QSR), Automotive, Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), or Retail. Benefits Work with a leading startup in a high-demand industry, and you would be working with like-minded experts aiming to transform video ad operations Competitive salary Comprehensive medical benefits (Medical, Vision, Dental, and Life Insurance) Cell phone and Wi-Fi reimbursement Gym Stipend Bill Spend Stipend Work-life flexibility – we value your contributions above all About Channel Factory Founded in 2010, Channel Factory is an award-winning marketing technology company that helps top global brands and agencies maximize video advertising across YouTube, CTV, and social platforms. Recognized as a technology innovator by Cynopsis and one of the fastest-growing companies by Inc., Channel Factory has served over three hundred of the Fortune 500 in delivering scalable, brand-safe, contextually aligned advertising software and services. By tapping into the deepest proprietary data pool on the market, the company enables highly customized, contextually aware, and dynamically optimized campaigns that deliver industry-leading performance for a portfolio of clients across all sectors. Channel Factory is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. Base Salary Range: $135,000-145,000

jobs.title: Field Marketing Manager
jobs.description: The Role Clearstory is hiring a Field Marketing Manager to own our trade show presence, customer events, field campaigns, gifting programs, and webinars from idea to full execution. This is a builder role for someone who can take a concept and turn it into a flawlessly run program — and who is just as comfortable owning a budget and a ROI number as they are running a booth on-site. You'll report to the VP of Marketing and work in close partnership with Sales, Partnerships, RevOps, and Content to make sure every program generates real pipeline, not just activity. You'll be judged on outcomes: MQLs generated, pipeline sourced and influenced, and — most importantly — how much of that pipeline converts into paid customers. What Great Looks Like Someone who can turn a vague idea into a fully executed program without a lot of hand-holding — strong at both the creative front end (what should we do, and why) and the unglamorous back end (shipping logistics, budget tracking, follow-up cadence). Detail-oriented enough to run flawless on-site execution, and analytical enough to walk into a leadership review with a clean ROI story for every dollar spent. Why This Role Own a complete function — field marketing is yours to build, run, and be measured on Direct visibility with GTM leadership on pipeline and revenue impact, not just activity A company culture built on our values: Be Curious, Keep It Simple, Customer Obsession, Raise the Bar What You'll Do Trade Shows & Industry Events Own the annual trade show and conference calendar — which events we show up at, at what tier, and why Manage end-to-end logistics: booth design and vendor coordination, shipping, staffing, swag, and on-site execution Prep the sales team attending with talk tracks, target account lists, and a lead capture process Build a repeatable pre-show / on-site / post-show playbook Customer & Field Events Plan and run regional customer events, dinners, happy hours, and executive roundtables Partner with Sales and Customer Success on the account list for each event Own venue, format, guest experience, and follow-up end to end Field Marketing Campaigns Take a campaign from initial idea to a fully scoped plan — audience, message, channel mix, budget, timeline — and run it Build account-based and regional campaigns combining direct mail, gifting, digital, and in-person touches Coordinate with Content and Demand Gen so field campaigns reinforce the broader marketing calendar Gifting Campaigns Design and run always-on and campaign-specific gifting motions targeted at key accounts and champions Own the gifting vendor/platform relationship, budget, and approval workflow Tie every gifting send to a clear trigger and a defined next step for the rep Measurement, ROI & Reporting Instrument every program with proper source/campaign tracking before it launches Report on MQLs generated, pipeline created and influenced, and conversion to closed-won Calculate program-level ROI (cost per MQL, cost per pipeline dollar, cost per closed-won customer) and use it to decide what to scale, fix, or cut Bring a monthly field marketing scorecard to GTM leadership Requirements 3-6+ years in field marketing or event marketing ideally at a B2B SaaS company BA/BS degree or equivalent experience preferred. A track record of planning and executing trade shows, customer events, and campaigns end to end — not just supporting them Experience running gifting programs and webinar series as part of a pipeline-generation motion Comfortable owning a budget and being measured on ROI: MQLs, pipeline sourced/influenced, and conversion to closed-won Strong project management skills — can juggle multiple programs at different stages without dropping details Hands-on with marketing/RevOps tooling (HubSpot or similar CRM, gifting platforms, webinar platforms) and comfortable setting up UTM/source tracking Excellent cross-functional collaborator — this role only works in close partnership with Sales, Partnerships, RevOps, and Content Construction, AEC, or another complex B2B industry background is a plus, not a requirement Excellent communication skills with internal and external customers as well as vendors and partners Willing and able to travel for events Must be in the Bay Area and in office 3 days a week About You We want you to be a part of the Clearstory success story so as you engage with us and our team members, it would be helpful for you to understand some of the core characteristics of our team - hopefully many of these resonate with you! Embody our core values Be Curious Customer Obsession Keep It Simple Raise the bar Passion and enthusiasm for your work and the Company Loves to take the initiative An upbeat, positive and good-to-be-around attitude. Sense of humor. Is a “doer” with a hands-on approach Very high energy. Commitment to excellence. Operationally focused - thinking about the entire business and not just your role. Bright, quick, articulate, able to influence without direct authority, excellent presentation and interpersonal skills, and able to adapt to different outside constituencies. Ability to influence peers, operational managers, and executive team. People willingly seek out your advice in the planning phase of decisions. Strong entrepreneurial nature and approach. You foster trust and accessibility. Strong prioritization skills. Aggressive drive with a can-do attitude. Ability to build relationships and earn the respect of other teams. Organizational tolerance: able to work with ambiguity and constant change. Genuine passion for customer service. Enjoys and has implemented change. Believes strongly in his/her abilities. Benefits The Company You’ll Join We are a first-of-its-kind, category-defining software that is revolutionizing the commercial construction industry. Clearstory is digitizing and automating the change order process inside the commercial construction industry. Regardless of what financial software a construction company uses internally, they can use us to share costs with the companies they work with. Just as TurboTax did for tax documents and Bill.com did for accounts receivable and accounts payable, Clearstory is doing the same for change order communication between construction companies. The construction industry is being transformed fast by technology, but the way companies communicate costs hasn’t evolved in decades and still heavily relies on carbon copy paper, spreadsheets, and email to track billions of dollars. These arcane manual processes can take days or weeks and include hours of manual office tasks such as scanning, manually transcribing, and tedious data entry into spreadsheets. At Clearstory we are changing that and creating a new category “change order communication,” by intelligently digitizing this age-old process. This leads to an increase in profits, more successful contractor-to-customer relationships, more transparency into a project’s true cost, and less wasted paper! We are a Series B 100% SaaS company with impressive credentials for a company at our stage. The Team You’ll be Surrounded by In addition to experienced SaaS sales, marketing, engineering, and product leaders, our team has over 60 years of combined experience in the commercial construction space. At Clearstory we know our customer’s pain points and challenges firsthand and have built a category-defining product that serves the user first. You’ll be part of an ambitious and collaborative company, committed to growing a supportive and diverse team that is passionate about empowering our contractor customers. More important than meeting 100% of qualifications, we are looking for collaborative, long-term team members with a growth mindset, a commitment to proactive communication, and a bias towards action, who are aligned and excited with our company’s mission to build the industry standard in digital change order communication for the commercial construction industry. The Opportunity As an early member of the team, you will have an exceptional level of impact on the development and iteration of our Company and the workplace culture itself. This is your chance to join a team that is bringing game-changing technology to a stagnant, static, pen-and-paper part of the commercial construction industry. This is an earlier-stage company and as such you will have many intangible benefits that go along with that opportunity such as the ability to influence the culture of your workplace, the ability to make an immediate impact with a product that already has an established product market fit and a healthy and growing user base as well as significant product influence. jobs.title: Paid Search Strategist, DTC eCommerce (Remote)
jobs.description: Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. That is the whole job. Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business. So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face. At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero. You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end. Here is what "end to end" actually means. You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result. You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme. You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number. You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output. If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast. If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading. Requirements What the job looks like Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month. Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working. Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people. Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing. Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target. Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule. Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery. Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why. Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team. Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt. You are a fit if You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search. You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have. You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list. You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard. You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you. Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too. You are not a fit if "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed. You want to be told what to do this week. You need a ticketing system to know what matters. You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question. Benefits Why this role is exciting This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency. You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale. You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident. You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

jobs.description: Job Description As a pivotal leader on Zendesk’s Marketing Strategy & Operations team, the Director of Marketing Analytics will turn marketing data into better decisions, stronger investment choices, and measurable business outcomes. This role sets the vision for marketing measurement and insights across the funnel, bringing together performance reporting, attribution, forecasting, experimentation, data quality, and executive storytelling. What you’ll be doing Lead and develop a high-performing Marketing Analytics team focused on measurement, insights, performance management, forecasting, attribution, engineering, and decision support. Define and evolve the marketing measurement strategy, including standardized KPI definitions, reporting governance, funnel health, channel performance, and ROI frameworks. Build trusted, scalable analytics products and self-service dashboards that give Marketing and senior leaders timely visibility into performance and opportunities. Partner with Finance, Sales/Revenue Operations, Data/Engineering, Product, and Marketing leaders on planning, target setting, pipeline pacing, budget allocation, and business reviews. Advance attribution and incrementality approaches, connecting campaign and channel activity to pipeline, revenue, customer outcomes, and investment decisions. Create a culture of insight generation: frame the business question, identify the right evidence, explain the implications, and recommend what to do next. Establish data quality, semantic-layer, documentation, and governance practices that make analytics reliable, reusable, and understandable across teams. Translate complex analytical findings into concise narratives and recommendations for executives and non-technical stakeholders. What you bring to the role A commercially minded analytics leader who cares as much about decision quality and business impact as methodological rigor. The ability to move from ambiguous business questions to clear analytical plans, useful outputs, and decisive recommendations. Strong executive presence and storytelling skills, with the ability to make complex data accessible without oversimplifying it. A collaborative leadership style that builds trust with Marketing, Finance, Sales/RevOps, Data, and technical partners. Curiosity and healthy skepticism: you test assumptions, explain uncertainty, and distinguish signal from noise. A talent developer who can raise the team’s analytical craft while keeping work connected to the highest-value business priorities. Willingness to leverage Agentic Analytics and deliver self-service analytics capabilities to stakeholders. Qualifications 10+ years of experience in marketing analytics, business intelligence, performance analytics, strategy, or a related discipline, including experience leading teams. Proven experience with marketing measurement, attribution, forecasting, experimentation, channel or campaign performance, and ROI analysis. Strong SQL and data-modeling fluency, with experience working across a data warehouse (Snowflake, AWS,etc), BI/dashboarding environments (Tableau, Streamlit, etc), and data management systems (SelectStar, Informatica, etc) Experience integrating marketing, web, advertising, CRM, and revenue data into trusted reporting and decision frameworks. Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive action from analytical insights. Experience in a high-growth B2B SaaS or similarly complex global marketing environment preferred. The US annualized base salary range for this position is $203,000.00-$305,000.00. This position may also be eligible for bonus, benefits, or related incentives.
