jobs.description: Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country. Deployed by over 85 health plans, including many of the top 20, and representing more than 270 million lives, Machinify brings together a fully configurable and content-rich, AI-powered platform along with best-in-class expertise. We’re constantly reimagining what’s possible in our industry, creating disruptively simple, powerfully clear ways to maximize financial outcomes and drive down healthcare costs. About the Opportunity   We are seeking a motivated and hands-on Product Marketing Manager to support the development of our product marketing function as Machinify evolves from services-based offerings to a unified, scalable tech platform model.  This is a builder role for someone excited to learn by doing. You will work closely with Product Marketing leadership and cross-functional partners to build foundational assets, support product launches, and help translate complex capabilities into clear, compelling messaging. You’ll play a key role in improving how our products are understood by customers and enabling sales and go-to-market success.   Key Responsibilities & Skillsets Messaging & Positioning (Support & Execution) Assist in developing and refining product messaging, positioning, and value propositions across the platform –so buyers and the people who influence them understand “why Machinify” and “why now.” Translate complex AI-powered capabilities into clear, defensible value propositions for payer audiences (executive, clinical, operations, and payment integrity). Partner with product, sales, and operations teams to incorporate feedback into messaging and content. Persona Development & Customer Insight Support the development of personas by gathering and synthesizing customer, sales, and market insights. Help map customer pain points and workflows across the payment integrity lifecycle. Partner with product, sales, and operations teams to incorporate feedback into messaging and content. Video-Forward Storytelling & Core Asset Library Support video content development, including scripting, coordinating with subject matter experts, and working with creative teams. Potential output includes product explainers, “what it is/why it matters” modules, release highlights, and buyer-specific narratives that reduce time-to-understanding. Contribute to the creation of core marketing assets such as product collateral, sales enablement materials, and short-form content. Ensure content aligns with overall product messaging and clearly communicates customer value. Product Launches Assist in coordinating product launches in partnership with Product Operations and Marketing. Help develop launch materials, internal communications, and enablement resources. Support execution of repeatable launch processes and post-launch learnings. Sales Enablement Help create and maintain sales tools such as pitch decks, one-pagers, and competitive insights. Work with sales teams to understand common objections and areas where messaging can improve. Contribute to training and enablement efforts to support field teams. What You Bring (role requirements)   Experience Experience in product marketing (or adjacent GTM roles with heavy messaging/content ownership), ideally in B2B SaaS and/or healthcare technology companies. Demonstrated experience supporting messaging, content creation, or product launches in a cross-functional environment. Experience partnering closely with product, operational, and sales counterparts. Personal Attributes Builder Mentality: Energized by creating the first version of what “great” looks like, and then iterating quickly as you learn. High Ownership, Low Ego: Jumps in wherever needed, seeks truth over credit, and prioritizes outcomes over optics. Technical Fluency: Able to engage product and data science teams to understand what’s real, what’s differentiated, and what needs nuance, and then translate it for market impact. Clarity Obsessed: Unusually strong instinct for simplifying complexity into language that moves decisions and reduces friction. Credible, Customer-Focused Storytelling: Balances ambition with accuracy; aims for defensible, trustworthy narratives in a high-stakes healthcare context. Comfort with Ambiguity: Thrives in a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve as Machinify scales its unified platform approach. Additional Requirements Experience building and scaling product marketing “from the ground up” is strongly preferred. Passion for healthcare technology and commitment to improving outcomes through smarter, more accurate systems. This comprehensive set of requirements is designed to attract candidates who can effectively lead the product marketing function as Machinify brings our legacy companies together and transitions to a tech-first product model.  This is an exempt position. We help US local governments and school districts plan, budget, report, and communicate their finances with clarity and confidence. From long-term planning to financial reporting, compliance, and transparency, our platform connects the work finance teams are already doing and makes it easier to deliver for their communities. Today, more than 2,000 public sector organizations use ClearGov, and we continue to expand our platform and reach as we grow. Our Core Values Be Clear & Credible  We are authentic in our interactions, communicating with clarity, speaking with honesty, and following through with consistency. We turn transparency into our greatest competitive advantage.  Be Human   We are human partners to our colleagues and customers and lead with consideration and kindness - making space for others to do the same. We turn empathy into a shared strength. Be Better Together   We are committed to building an inclusive community where everyone thrives. We share successes, support each other through challenges, and show up for our teammates the way we show up for our customers. We turn togetherness into our greatest advantage and collaboration into our greatest multiplier. Be Honourable/Honorable   We are responsible to our colleagues and customers. We bring our full selves to every conversation, every project, every decision, and every relationship. We act with intention, deliver on our commitments, and lead with integrity - even when no one is watching. We turn honour into the foundation that powers everything we do. Be Connected We are culture builders where people are seen, welcomed, and celebrated. We show up in every interaction - the laughs, the wins, the hard days. We turn connection into opportunities for people to feel they belong. What Makes You a Great Fit You take ownership and follow through You communicate clearly and effectively You're comfortable solving problems and figuring things out You learn quickly and adapt as things change You care about the team, not just your own work You bring a sense of humor and perspective to what you do About the Opportunity ClearGov has built a strong product marketing foundation, with an established team supporting product launches, messaging, and sales enablement across a growing portfolio. As the company enters its next phase of growth, ClearGov is hiring a Director of Product & Solution Marketing to elevate the function from strong product-level execution to platform-and- solution-level strategy. Reporting to the VP of Marketing, this leader will define how ClearGov positions, packages, and brings to market a suite of 13 products across cities, counties, school districts, and special districts, each with distinct needs and buying dynamics. The Director of Product & Solution Marketing will help the company make sharper decisions about where to invest, how the products fit together, and how ClearGov expands within its customer base. This is a highly visible leadership role with meaningful autonomy and direct access to the executive team and board. The Director of Product & Solution Marketing will serve as a strategic partner to the VP of Marketing, CPO and CRO, translating customer and market insight into portfolio choices and measurable commercial impact. This leader will manage an established team of four, creating a five-person product & solution marketing organization, with the opportunity to grow the team as the function expands. Key Responsibilities: Lead pricing and packaging strategy: Set the strategic direction for bundling, discounting, and launch pricing in partnership with Product, Finance, Revenue, and external research partners. Set portfolio and commercialization strategy: Define how ClearGov’s products fit together, where bundling and cross-sell opportunities exist, and how positioning and go-to-market motions should vary across customer segments. Shape executive decision-making: Represent product marketing with the executive team and board, connecting market, customer, and competitive insight to growth priorities and business performance. Lead and develop the product marketing organization: Build on the team’s subject matter expertise and strengths in messaging, launches, and enablement while expanding its capabilities in portfolio strategy, market intelligence, pricing, and commercial planning. Build a scalable launch and integration model: Partner with Product, Marketing, and Sales on new product / bundle launches and create repeatable approaches for positioning, packaging, and commercializing acquired products. Strengthen expansion motions: Partner with Revenue and Marketing leaders to improve cross-sell, upsell, and account-based growth programs across ClearGov’s customer base. Establish a market and customer intelligence discipline: Build competitive intelligence, win-loss analysis, and industry engagement that inform product, sales, and portfolio decisions. Own the market narrative and field adoption: Craft bold, outcome-based messaging that clearly differentiates ClearGov from spreadsheets and competing vendors, including sharp depositioning that sales can use in live deals. Ensure sales actually uses what the team builds by measuring content adoption, retiring assets that go unused, and tying messaging to win rates. Create clear measures of impact: Define how product marketing performance is evaluated and connect the team’s work to adoption, expansion, win rates, and revenue outcomes. Critical Skills/Experience: Significant product marketing leadership experience in B2B SaaS, including recent experience at the Director or Senior Director level, or operating at a comparable scope. Experience owning go-to-market or commercialization strategy across a multi-product / platform portfolio, multiple customer segments, or distinct buyer personas. Pricing and packaging experience, including bundling, discounting, or launch pricing. A track record of translating customer, market, and competitive insight into positioning, portfolio, investment, or growth decisions. People leadership experience, including building, developing, and elevating a product marketing team. Strong partnership with Product, Sales, and Marketing leaders in a mid-market or enterprise sales environment. Executive presence and sound judgment, with the ability to operate autonomously, align senior stakeholders, and communicate strategy clearly to executives and board members. Comfort operating in a growing, evolving business where portfolio priorities and organizational needs continue to change. Experience with mid-market or lower-enterprise B2B SaaS products in the $30K–$60K ARR range and sales cycles of approximately three to four months. Preferred Skills/Experience: Experience with programmatic growth motions such as account-based marketing, cross-sell, or upsell at scale. Experience with enterprise SaaS products of $75k-$250M+ Background in GovTech, FinTech, finance, accounting, compliance, or another technical or regulated vertical. Experience supporting growth through M&A, portfolio expansion, or product-line integration. Experience building win-loss, competitive intelligence, or industry analyst programs. jobs.description: Keep Growing with Nutrafol We’re a growing company. Everything we do, we do to help people grow into the best version of themselves. As the pioneers of hair wellness, we create clinically tested products for hair growth and provide support for people at every step of their hair journey. Our multi-factorial approach targets key root causes of hair thinning using a patented blend of standardized vitamins, minerals and natural ingredients -- and is recommended by over 7,500 physicians and hair professionals for trusted, reliable results. We never settle, and are continuously challenging existing treatments and methodologies to advance the frontier of hair science. As we help our customers grow, we grow too -- by embracing individuality and differences, leading by example, and empowering ourselves and others with our passion for wellness and innovation. Keep growing. It’s our mantra. Our commitment to helping anybody and everybody committed to realizing their own potential to grow. About You: The Director, Brand Marketing, Nutrafol will build and launch the brand story for new product innovations! Nutrafol is the #1 dermatologist-recommended hair growth supplement brand and the pioneer of the hair wellness category. We’re in the process of developing new product innovation that extends our focus from the inside-out to the outside-in. Your job is to make the range unmistakably Nutrafol  - why it exists, who it's for, how it fits the routine she's already in, and why she should believe it works. You'll partner closely with Product Development, who owns formulation, claims substantiation, and the Unilever R&D and Supply relationship. You bring the consumer into that work: the insight that shapes what we make and the plan that gets it into her hands. This is a builder's role. turn competitive and category analysis into a point of view, not a deck Identify the insights and tensions that shape both the launch and the next wave of innovation Own naming for the range and individual SKUs, working with Creative, with Legal and Product Development holding sign-off on trademark availability and claims risk Product Partnership Bring consumer insight and brand POV into the product pipeline - feed the proposition, format, and range decisions that Product Development owns Deliver a ranked consumer-priority claims input ahead of study protocol design, so Product Development and R&D can prioritize what gets tested and substantiated Own how approved claims show up in market — which ones lead, how they're expressed, how they ladder to the story Shape the launch range and wave sequencing as a required consumer input into Product Development's range recommendation Protect the brand across every consumer-facing touchpoint, holding the line on the dermatologist-recommended credibility and the subscription model that built us Launch and Go-To-Market Build the launch plan across DTC, Amazon, and Pro in partnership with Growth, Marketplaces, CX, and Pro Marketing Accountable for launch readiness and in-market performance against the agreed product availability date, which Product Development owns Own new product innovation pricing above an agreed margin floor set annually with Finance Lead the annual and quarterly brand plan for new product innovation, with clear priorities and a roadmap the cross-functional team can work from Brief and collaborate with Creative; lead ideation on campaign, content, and social narrative Set the brand direction for partnerships, collaborations, and any external voices attached to the range Manage the new product innovation brand marketing budget Leadership without authority Keep a cross-company group moving to one plan - and know which decisions are yours, which are Product's, and which need both Own the consumer, positioning, and go-to-market sections of Unilever leadership updates, delivered from one shared plan alongside Product Development Give clear, executive-ready updates to Nutrafol leadership Surface risks and dependencies early rather than reporting them after the fact Track performance post-launch and use what you learn to sharpen the range and inform what comes next Build trust fast across teams who've never worked on a launch like this Requirements: 8–12 years of brand management, brand marketing, or innovation marketing at a high-growth brand; hair care, beauty, or science-led consumer health preferred. DTC experience is required Track record taking a product from concept to market alongside R&D, regulatory, and supply chain - you don't need to have run formulation, but you need to know how to be a good partner to the people who do Proven ability to build integrated brand strategies and launch campaigns across digital, social, CRM, retail media, and direct response Strong commercial and go-to-market instincts across DTC, e-commerce, and omnichannel, including pricing Comfortable at the seam between an entrepreneurial brand and a large matrixed organization, and able to align partners across both without formal authority Fluent in segmentation and in both quantitative and qualitative consumer insight Sharp judgment on claims, positioning, and premium experience Entrepreneurial and self-directed - you'll be hands-on doing the work, not just directing it Exceptional written and verbal communication Low ego, high ownership, and the kind of energy that makes a dispersed team want to be in the room Nutrafol takes into consideration a wide range of factors in final compensation decisions, including but not limited to: skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, qualifications and education, and other business and organizational needs. jobs.title: Customer Advocacy Marketing Manager
jobs.description: About AlphaSense:  The world’s most sophisticated companies rely on AlphaSense to remove uncertainty from decision-making. With market intelligence and search built on proven AI, AlphaSense delivers insights that matter from content you can trust. Our universe of public and private content includes equity research, company filings, event transcripts, expert calls, news, trade journals, and clients’ own research content. The acquisition of Tegus by AlphaSense in 2024 advances our shared mission to empower professionals to make smarter decisions through AI-driven market intelligence. Together, AlphaSense and Tegus will accelerate growth, innovation, and content expansion, with complementary product and content capabilities that enable users to unearth even more comprehensive insights from thousands of content sets. Our platform is trusted by over 6,000 enterprise customers, including a majority of the S&P 500. Founded in 2011, AlphaSense is headquartered in New York City with more than 2,000 employees across the globe and offices in the U.S., U.K., Finland, India, Singapore, Canada, and Ireland. Come join us! About the Role:  The Customer Advocacy Marketing Manager owns both the strategy and scaled production of customer proof-point content: case studies, customer quotes and testimonials, logo usage and compliance, and the customer reviews program (G2, Gartner Peer Insights, TrustRadius). This role also owns the Customer Awards program, on-site customer content capture (video/filming) at flagship events, and the review-platform vendor relationships and budget. The ideal candidate can set a proof-point content roadmap and prioritize it against business impact, not just execute a queue — while also running a high-volume content operation end-to-end, from sourcing through legal and customer approval. This role partners closely with our Senior Manager who owns high-touch programs like our CAB, Executive Sponsorship, RKO, and customer community. Proven track record of owning content projects end-to-end, including legal/compliance coordination. Experience owning vendor relationships and budget, ideally for review-generation or reference platforms. Strong written communication skills and an eye for turning customer insight into compelling assets. Determine which customer stories, quotes, and proof points to pursue based on expected pipeline, bookings, and adoption impact, rather than a first-in-first-out intake queue. jobs.description: Twin Health  At Twin Health, we empower people to improve and prevent chronic metabolic diseases, like type 2 diabetes and obesity, with a new standard of care. Twin Health is the only company applying AI Digital Twin technology exclusively toward metabolic health.  We start by building a dynamic model of each person’s metabolism — drawing on thousands of data points from CGMs, smartwatches, and meal logs — that maps their personal path to better health. Guided by a dedicated clinical care team, our members have lowered their A1C below the diabetes range, achieved lasting weight loss, and reduced or even eliminated medications, all while living healthier, happier lives. Working here  Our team at Twin Health is passionate, talented, and united by a shared purpose: to improve the metabolic health and happiness of our members. We believe in empowering every Twin to make a meaningful impact for our members, our clients, and each other, while enjoying a supportive, collaborative work environment. Twin has been recognized not only for our innovation but also for our culture, including: Innovator of the Year by the Employer Health Innovation Roundtable (EHIR), selected to CB Insights’ Digital Health 150, and named one of Newsweek’s Top Most Loved Workplace® . With more than $100 million raised in recent funding, including a $53 million Series E round in 2025 led by Maj Invest, and a $50 million investment in 2023 led by Temasek, Twin is scaling rapidly across the U.S. and globally. Backed by leading venture firms like ICONIQ Growth, Sequoia, Sofina, Temasek, and Peak XV, we are building the most impactful digital health company in the world. Join us as we reinvent the standard of care in metabolic health.   Opportunity Today, Twin Health does almost no proactive marketing to our active members. Once someone enrolls, nearly every communication they receive is either a product-triggered push notification or a message from their care team. That has taken us a long way — but it leaves an entire layer of engagement unbuilt. We are hiring our first Active Member Marketing Manager to build that layer. You will own the strategy and the execution of every proactive, non-clinically led communication a Twin member receives: email, SMS, in-app and push campaigns, direct mail testing, member webinars, and additional channel exploration we have not yet tried. You will design how those communications layer into the care team relationship and the product notification ecosystem already in place. This is a build role requiring both strategic vision as well as executional know how. Twin members, data, clinical outcomes, and Braze infrastructure is already in place. What does not exist is a deliberate lifecycle program. You will write the strategy, then ship it yourself. We are looking for someone who can point to campaigns they personally built and outcomes they personally moved. Responsibilities  Active Member Strategy and Program Ownership Map the member journey to build sustained engagement, as well as winback for lapsed members, and define the communication strategy for each stage, including who we deliberately choose not to message. Own the annual and quarterly engagement roadmap, with a defined direction on stage involvement  Build a segmentation model grounded in real member behavior, sensors, app engagement, care team interaction, clinical trajectory, enrollment channels, etc.  Govern the member communication calendar across marketing, care team, product, and clinical, so members experience one coherent voice instead of four uncoordinated ones. Integration with the Care Team and Product Ecosystem Inventory the existing touchpoint landscape and maintain that map as the source of truth. Partner with Care Delivery and Clinical leadership to define the boundary between a marketing communication and a clinical one. Member marketing should make the care team more effective, not compete with it for attention. Design suppression, frequency capping, and quiet-hours logic across all channels so total message volume stays deliberate as the program scales. Work with Product on campaign-based push and in-app messaging Ensure deployment accuracy by accounting for the operational realities of the point solution ecosystem: eligibility files, employer and health plan communication rules, benefits calendars, co-branding constraints, and the fact that our members are often being messaged by three other vendors the same week. Execution, Platform, and Analysis Build and ship campaigns end to end in Braze: audience logic, Canvas and journey build, content, QA, launch, and iteration. Write copy and creative briefs, and manage design, clinical and legal review as needed to deliver timely campaigns on schedule. Develop the Braze instance as it matures: event taxonomy, catalog and Connected Content usage, template library, preference center, deliverability and sender reputation, and the data contract with our Snowflake warehouse. Stand up a formal testing program: subject lines and creative to start, then channel mix, cadence, timing, incentive structure, and a direct mail pilot  Measure performance and build dashboard in partnership with Marketing operations to showcase campaign efficacy Report results to Growth Marketing and the broader leadership team on a regular cadence, including wins, losses and adjustments as a result. Maintain compliance discipline throughout — HIPAA, PHI handling, TCPA and consent management for SMS, CAN-SPAM, and internal clinical review.  Other duties as assigned Qualifications  Required 4–7 years in lifecycle, CRM, retention, or engagement marketing, with meaningful time spent owning programs end to end rather than executing someone else’s brief. Hands-on Braze expertise. You can build a multi-branch Canvas with behavioral triggers, Liquid personalization, and proper suppression logic without waiting on engineering. Real multi-channel experience including email plus at least one of SMS, push, or in-app Demonstrated experimentation rigor: you design tests with holdouts, understand what a result can and cannot support, and are comfortable reporting a null. Comfort building and defining processes. This program does not exist yet; you will be building the first version. Strongly Preferred Healthcare or digital health experience, with working fluency in HIPAA and PHI handling in marketing systems. Direct experience in the point solution ecosystem: a digital health, condition management, or benefits vendor distributed through employers, health plans, or health systems. You understand eligibility-driven populations, client communication approvals, and the practical difference between enrollment marketing and active member marketing. Experience marketing alongside a human care team or clinical staff Exposure to offline or physical channels (direct mail, print, or member webinars) and how to measure them. How We Will Measure Success Channel metrics matter, but they are not the scoreboard. In the first year, this role will be evaluated on: Member activation:  speed and rate of getting new members fully onboarded and using the program as designed. Retention — reduced member attrition  Clinical outcomes — increased milestone achievements directly impact the bottom line for Twin. Program maturity — a functioning lifecycle engine: documented strategy, healthy deliverability, a running test backlog, and reporting the business trusts. Lead status date stamps, speed to lead tracking, etc.) Sales performance & activity reports Operational and day-to-day SOP creation for CRM utilization and clean data entry Support internal growth of the Marketing Ops Department Audit systems of prospective/existing clients Actively identify opportunities to improve products/services beyond their accounts  Mentors team members and holds strategy sessions on accounts they support with  Reviews and provides feedback to junior team members on reports & deliverables  Assist with developing our product offering, identify opportunities to improve the department, and actively share insights with the team Document all processes and conduct trainings for client and/or sales team members Requirements: 4+ years experience in marketing operations or related role Expert in Hubspot and proficient in Pardot (any other MAP and CRM platforms are a plus!) High proficiency in Salesforce with the ability to perform intermediate functions including but not limited to: Report and dashboard-builds Campaign setup and reporting Field setup and mapping Record customization Intermediate to advanced automation builds Experience with various sales and marketing systems and tools (ie. ZoomInfo, SalesLoft, Insycle, 6Sense, etc.) and an understanding of how they interact and integrate with a Marketing Automation Platform and/or CRM Ability to quickly troubleshoot issues within the marketing technology stack (including the CRM) Experience building out complex processes and automations  Ability to be client-facing and discuss complex strategies and recommendations with the client  Comfortable with ambiguity. jobs.description: Array is a financial innovation platform that helps digital brands, financial institutions, and fintechs get compelling consumer products to market faster. We deliver a suite of credit and identity monitoring tools, privacy protection, and a financial ads marketplace via embeddable widgets or a clean, modern API. Our private label offerings help drive revenue and increase engagement for our customers while empowering millions of consumers to achieve their financial goals. As a remote-first company, we’re focused on providing opportunities for high performing individuals to have deep impact in the fast growing fintech space. A clear mission, a commitment to continuous improvement and a willingness to experiment empower us individually and together deliver the best products for our clients and users. As a Digital Marketing Manager at Array, you will be our in-house performance marketing engine — you do what a full-service agency would do, except you sit inside the GTM team, know our verticals, and are accountable to pipeline. This role reports to the Head of Marketing. The role You’re the person in the ad platforms, in the CMS, in the analytics. Every program you run has a goal attached: net new customers, retention, or land-and-expand. If it can’t be tied to one of those, it doesn’t run. You will: Paid media — strategy and execution. Own Google Ads and LinkedIn end to end: account structure, budgets, bids, audiences, creative testing, and performance. Targeting aligned to our Tier 1/Tier 2 must-get accounts and five verticals. You build it, you run it, you hold the number. SEO and AI search — Build our organic program from a standing start: technical foundation, on-page work, keyword strategy mapped by vertical, and optimizing for how buyers actually search now (traditional rankings and AI/answer-engine visibility). You write the briefs; content production supports you. Top-of-funnel demand — Own the programs that fill the top of the funnel: search and social capture, content syndication, retargeting, and the paid layer under our ABM motion into must-get accounts. Landing pages and conversion —  Own the conversion layer of the site: landing pages, A/B testing, form and funnel optimization, and our Qualified chatbot (routing through Salesforce). You own what converts. Measurement —  Own tracking and reporting for everything above: UTM discipline, Salesforce campaign hygiene, and a pipeline-by-channel view.  Work in the platforms daily. No vendor sits between you and the data. Report digital’s contribution to pipeline by vertical, in the same terms sales uses. Cut spend on programs that aren’t working, including the ones you built. Act on what you find the same week when able — a new audience, a rebuilt page, a tracking fix. Maintain a habit of using AI tools to think, build, and ship faster — it’s your default, not an afterthought. Who you’ll work with Demand Gen, Sales and our Vertical Marketing Managers — your programs feed their pods, and account lists shape your targeting. Marketing Ops and RevOps — your partners on routing, attribution, and Salesforce campaign hygiene. What great looks like 90 days in: you own paid spend end to end — accounts audited, broken campaigns rebuilt, underperforming spend cut. Baseline SEO is in place (technical audit, keyword map by vertical, first briefs out) and testing is running on the top conversion paths. 6 months in: leadership uses your pipeline dashboard in planning. Organic traffic is growing. Sales can point to deals that started with a program you ran. You have: 5+ years running performance marketing hands-on for B2B, with real budget ownership — you’ve planned spend, defended it, and moved it when the data said to. Agency background is strongly welcome; you’ve run multiple client accounts and want to go deep on one. Platform fluency you can prove: Google Ads, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, GA4, Google Tag Manager, and a CRM/MAP stack (we run Salesforce and HubSpot; we also use, ZoomInfo, and Gong). Real SEO chops: you can run a technical audit, brief content, and explain search visibility — including AI search — to an executive without jargon. CRO experience with testing frameworks, not just hunches. A pipeline-first mindset: you talk in opportunities and revenue influenced, not just impressions. Strong project management and communication — you can run multiple campaigns and stakeholders at once with clear briefs, tight timelines, and no dropped threads. Comfort as a team of one with agency-sized scope — this is a build role in a fast-moving GTM org, and you’d rather own the whole engine than a slice of it. A belief that AI is reshaping work — you instinctively use it to accelerate everything you do: analysis, reporting, briefs, creative iteration. Our team builds this way; you should too. Nice to have: Fintech experience or selling into financial institutions. ABM platform experience and tiered account strategy. Experience marketing embedded/API products or private label offerings. Background in growth, social, or partner marketing alongside paid — you’ve pulled more than one lever. Experience with behavioral and intent data for targeting (we use ZoomInfo intent). Enough design/creative sense to brief ad creative well. Pay transparency: $160,000 + for base salary, depending on experience. Full time employee compensation includes an Incentive Stock Option (ISO) grant, subject to Board approval. Success means meeting defined performance standards through a six-month evaluation period — with continuous feedback and ongoing accountability as core parts of working at Array. Array Offers All Full Time Employees the following Benefits and Perks:  Full medical, dental, and vision, premiums covered at 100% for full-time employees and 70% for dependents Unlimited PTO and sick leave + 14 company holidays to encourage a healthy work-life blend 100% 401k match up to 4% with immediate vesting Generous and competitive parental leave for all parents $1,000 desk setup subsidy to set-up your unique remote office $100/month to subsidize wifi/cell phone expenses Summer Fridays (half-day Fridays) typically from late May to the end of August Commuter benefits for those who choose to go into our New York City or San Francisco office spaces Not sure if you meet the Qualifications? Come join our team and help us create secure cloud environments that allow even the best companies to move faster, all while having some fun! Experience marketing to technical audiences, with the ability to work with and market to technical security, cloud, and development personas within enterprises. This includes owning the product go to market strategy for one of our product areas, creating compelling messaging and positioning, launching new features, enabling the field teams, and partnering with marketing and revenue to target the right buyers and influencers. Become a subject matter expert in cloud security with an in-depth understanding of the market and products, including overall value proposition, features, functionality and the verticals and use cases in which they are relevant. jobs.title: Marketing Operations Specialist
jobs.description: Talkdesk competes in a market where the quality of execution separates companies that grow efficiently from those that spend more to get the same result. Marketing Operations is where that execution lives. This role exists to ensure that every dollar of marketing spend, every campaign, every event, and every account-based program translates into pipeline with zero friction. That requires a system built for precision where the right prospect reaches the right person at the right time, consistently and by design. You sit inside the Marketing team, with close partnerships across Sales and RevOps. The marketers running campaigns, events, and account-based programs are your primary stakeholders. When the system works, their work converts. In practice, that means owning the full operational surface of marketing technology: administering and continuously improving the tools that make up our GTM stack, building and maintaining the integrations that keep data moving cleanly between systems, designing the orchestrations that automate account and contact engagement, ensuring the enrichment and data integrity standards that make every downstream decision reliable. This is an interdependent system, and this person keeps it running as a coherent, high-performing whole. What You'll Own Account-Based Marketing Orchestration: Serve as the technical owner of our ABM orchestration layer. Translate signals from our intent platform into automated, sequenced actions across our marketing automation platform and CRM, working closely with campaign and field marketing teams to ensure the right programs reach the right accounts at the right moment. Getting this infrastructure right is one of the highest-impact contributions this role makes to the business. Marketing Technology Foundation: Own the day-to-day health of our martech systems and the workflows, API calls, integrations, and syncs that connect them to keep prospect data moving accurately through the funnel. When something breaks or underperforms, you diagnose it, fix it, and document the resolution so it does not recur. Agentic AI Workflow Engineering: Design and build automated workflows that use AI capabilities to evaluate qualitative signals, such as demo request notes, intent activity, and unstructured form inputs, alongside firmographic data to produce dynamic lead scores and routing decisions. You write the API calls, design the orchestration logic, test against edge cases, and iterate based on conversion outcomes. Experience shipping something to production is the bar. Enrichment and Insights: Build and manage the workflows that construct a complete, account-level intelligence profile from the moment a prospect engages. That means aggregating first-party behavioral signals, third-party intent data, firmographic context, and web research into a unified view that captures not just the individual contact but the broader buying committee: who across the account is engaging, with what content, and what their activity suggests about organizational priorities and pain points. That intelligence surfaces in the systems where sales and marketing work, so every follow-up is informed, relevant, and timed to the account's buying journey. System Documentation and Enablement: Every workflow you build or modify gets documented: field mapping dictionaries, AI orchestration logic, routing rule change logs. Beyond documentation, you actively invest in making the marketing team more self-sufficient, building self-service reporting and dashboards that allow marketers to check campaign performance, list quality, or lead status independently, and creating resources that allow colleagues to troubleshoot routine tasks and leverage AI tools without filing a request. An empowered marketing team operates with greater speed and confidence, and this role contributes meaningfully to that outcome. Who You Are You operate with a high degree of autonomy. You are embedded in the relevant standups, attentive to system performance, and typically ahead of issues before they surface as escalations. Your manager will set context and priorities; the execution is yours to own. You are invested in the success of the Marketing team. You understand that the campaigns, events, and programs your colleagues execute are only as effective as the systems that support them. Leads from a field event that go unrouted, an ABM sequence that executes against incomplete data, or a high-intent inbound request that experiences significant delay before reaching an SDR all represent measurable pipeline impact. You approach your work with that accountability in mind. You are technically strong and collaborative by nature. Marketers, Sales and RevOps are close partners. You understand their workflows well enough to anticipate where system gaps will affect their work, and communicate clearly when something is broken, when it is fixed, and why. Strong cross-functional relationships are central to this role. You see the work through to completion. You build, test, document, and close the loop. When something you own regresses, you identify it first. What We're Looking For Required 3 to 5 years in B2B SaaS Marketing Operations, Revenue Operations, or a systems-adjacent role Hands-on marketing automation and CRM administration, including configuring and maintaining MAP-to-CRM syncs Demonstrated ability to build and deploy an automated workflow that calls external APIs, whether webhooks, REST APIs, or LLM endpoints, in a production environment Native fluency in B2B funnel mechanics: MQL definitions, lifecycle stage transitions, opportunity lifecycles, and attribution models Experience coaching or enabling non-technical stakeholders on new tools, AI workflows, or self-service reporting Strong Signal Hands-on administrative experience with intent data platforms, routing engines, and ABM orchestration Prior experience building LLM-powered workflows for lead scoring, routing, or qualification Comfort reading and writing JSON, working with REST APIs, and debugging integration errors independently How We'll Measure Success The through-line across all of it is pipeline efficiency: more of the right prospects converting into pipeline from the programs already running, with less manual intervention and less fallout. 30 days: Full audit of marketing automation-to-CRM field mapping is complete, ownership of inbound routing rules is established, and current ABM workflow patterns are mapped to identify key automation opportunities. 60 days: First agentic AI workflow is deployed to staging or production. At least one major ABM orchestration sequence that previously required manual steps is automated. An initial self-service enablement resource or dashboard is delivered to the marketing team. 90 days and beyond: Lead sync exception rate is at target with a monitoring process that catches regressions before Sales does. ABM orchestration operates as a reliable service layer that campaign and field marketers can brief and trust to execute. Marketing colleagues actively leverage self-service tools and AI workflows independently. Application Question Required with your resume (200 words max): A high-intent prospect submits a demo request but never reaches the assigned SDR in the CRM. Walk us through your exact diagnostic process: which logs you check first, how you trace the break across the marketing automation-to-CRM sync and inbound routing rules, how you validate the fix, and how you would design an agentic step to evaluate the prospect's form submission notes for priority routing.     Pay Range (OTE Pay) : $86,000 - $144,000 Other Types of Pay : Based on level and role the employee may be eligible for long term incentives in the form of equity and short term incentives of either bonus or commission.  Health Insurance : Medical, Dental, Vision, Life and Disability Insurance, Employee Assistance Program (EAP). Retirement Benefits : 401(k) plan Paid Time Off : Talkdesk offers an uncapped paid time off program for exempt employees and an accrual-based program for non-exempt employees; both are subject to manager approval and consistent with business needs. Paid Holidays : Talkdesk offers 14 paid holidays each year.  Paid Sick Leave : Exempt employees have uncapped paid time off and non-exempt sick leave follows accrual standards; both are subject to manager approval and consistent with business needs. Method of Application : Apply online. Application Window : The application window is expected to close at least 10 days from the posting date. The application was posted on 09/25/2026. Benefits and perks listed above may vary based on the nature of your employment with Talkdesk. All questions or concerns about this posting should be directed to the Talent team at  Talent@talkdesk.com . Talkdesk is pioneering a new era of Customer Experience Automation (CXA), redefining how the world’s most admired brands interact with their customers through AI. Our global team of courageous innovators is customer-obsessed, building AI-first solutions that put empathy, trust, and transparency at the center of every interaction. We foster an inclusive culture where diverse perspectives drive our success and every voice belongs. Combining the stability of a global leader with the agility of a disruptor, Talkdeskers are empowered with the autonomy to drive meaningful impact, while giving back to the communities and environment around us. Talkdesk has been recognized as a Leader in the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) and in the G2 Overall Grid® Reports for AI Agents and Contact Center. With seven consecutive years on the Forbes Cloud 100 and multiple AI Breakthrough awards, there has never been a more exciting time to join us as we shape the future of customer experience automation! Work Environment and Physical Requirements: Primarily office-environment work, extended periods of sitting or standing, computer-based work. Limited lifting, and equipment usage limited to computer-related equipment (keyboards, mouse, etc.) The Talkdesk story hinges on empathy and acceptance. It is the shared goal among all Talkdeskers to empower a new kind of customer hero through our innovative software solution, and we firmly believe that the best path to success for our mission is inclusivity, diversity, and genuine acceptance. To that end, we will hire, promote, work along, cheer for, bond with, and warmly welcome into the Talkdesk family all persons without regard to ethnic and racial identity, indigenous heritage, national origin, religion, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, genetic information, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Demand Generation Marketing Manager
jobs.description: Who we are: Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks. Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector. Visit gomotive.com to learn more. What we’re looking for Demand Generation Marketing Manager: We're looking for someone who brings a marketer's curiosity and a builder's mindset to the Mid-Market segment. You understand the market we serve, the buyers you're reaching, and what moves them to act all while maintaining enthusiasm to solve challenges physical operations organizations face. You're always sharpening the axe: questioning assumptions, testing new approaches, growing your AI skill set and looking for ways to make the next campaign better than the last. You enjoy comfortable operating in ambiguity and a fast-paced environment where priorities shift and are not discouraged by blockers, but motivated to find solutions. If this sounds like you, read on!   Role Responsibilities Plan, execute, and optimize Programmatic ABM campaigns and full-funnel demand generation campaigns across dmid-market, and working with other segment leads to ensure large scale campaigns accurately capture ICP for all segments/personas.  Partner closely with the Content Marketing, Customer Marketing and PMM team to map existing content to the buyer's journey, identify content gaps, and request new content and sales collateral to support campaign objectives. Maintain target account lists and apply a working understanding of buyer funnel stages, definitions, and conversion benchmarks to inform targeting and messaging decisions. Partner with Marketing Operations to ensure accurate targeting, list hygiene, and campaign setup, flagging issues and driving resolution proactively. Collaborate with Product Marketing to apply established messaging frameworks to campaigns and adapt messaging for segment-specific needs. Develop campaign and creative briefs independently, including copy direction, messaging hierarchy, and design inputs that align to buyer journey stages. Campaign and ABM Execution Partner with channel owners to launch and monitor campaigns across: 6sense Display, LinkedIn, Additional Display channels, Content Syndication, Email, Web, Events/Field, Associations. You will not be responsible for hands on keyboard but work with partners to understand how each channel works individually and collectively to drive new pipeline across buying committees.  Own execution for select channels, including: Webinars, Calendared Sales Plays, and partnering on Direct Mail: managing end-to-end setup, targeting, launch, and performance tracking. Ensure channel execution aligns to defined campaign messaging and buyer journey stages, making adjustments based on performance data and segment feedback. Evaluate channel activations and performance and make strategic decisions based on segment and buyer needs, reallocating spend or effort when warranted. Build testing and iteration cycles into each campaign to gain a larger understanding of demand generation learnings.  Leverage AI tools and agentic workflows to accelerate campaign personalization, sales play development, and insight generation — applying a working knowledge of AI to streamline day-to-day execution without sacrificing quality. Sales Partnership and Enablement Partner with SDRs, AEs, and sales leadership to align marketing campaigns with outbound and inbound motions, ensuring marketing programs support sales priorities and pipeline goals. Enable sales teams to act on campaign engagement by providing targeting direction, messaging, sales plays, and enablement materials. Maintain regular communication with sales partners to share campaign performance, upcoming programs, and recommended actions, and to incorporate sales feedback into campaign planning. Contribute to weekly sales communications that summarize active marketing initiatives, upcoming programs, and sales actions. Prepare materials for sales meetings and planning sessions, tailoring content to the audience. Attend select sales meetings to stay aligned on priorities and feedback, advocating for marketing programs and incorporating sales input into campaign planning. Reporting and Optimization Monitor campaign performance and pipeline contribution against goals, identifying trends, risks, and optimization opportunities independently. Partner with Marketing Analytics to maintain dashboards and reporting cadences; partner with Marketing Operations and Sales Operations to maintain Outreach dashboards and sales command centers in Salesforce.  Analyze performance data to understand what is working and why, making recommendations for reallocation or adjustment. Contribute to weekly Mid-Market metrics updates with clear, actionable insights. Support ad-hoc reporting needs for WBRs, MBRs, and QBRs as requested, translating data into recommendations for leadership. Qualifications 5+ years of experience in B2B demand generation, campaign management, or growth marketing (not including internships). Proven track record of executing multi-channel demand generation campaigns that drive measurable pipeline contribution beyond just events. Hands-on experience with ABM strategies, including 1:Few and 1:Many campaign motions. Experience partnering with sales teams (SDRs, AEs) to align marketing campaigns with outbound and inbound motions. Working knowledge of marketing automation platforms and CRM systems (Salesforce, Marketo) Comfortable analyzing campaign performance data in Excel/Google Sheets and Tableau, with the ability to derive insights and make data-informed decisions. Strong project management skills with experience in Asana or equivalent tools. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to create compelling campaign briefs and sales enablement materials. Experience required: Salesforce (required), Asana, Sendoso (or equivalent), Outreach. Glean, Clay (preferred) Location Preference: Austin, TX, Nashville TN or San Francisco (2x a week in the office); however for the right candidate we will consider remote USA  This is an individual contributor role  Pay Transparency Your compensation may be based on several factors, including education, work experience, and certifications. For certain roles, total compensation may include restricted stock units. Motive offers benefits including health, pharmacy, optical and dental care benefits, paid time off, sick time off, short term and long term disability coverage, life insurance as well as 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). Learn more about our benefits by visiting Motive Perks & Benefits . The compensation range for this position will depend on where you reside. For this role, the compensation range is: United States $90,000 — $111,000 USD Creating a diverse and inclusive workplace is one of Motive's core values. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives.  Please review our Candidate Privacy Notice  here . UK Candidate Privacy Notice here . The applicant must be authorized to receive and access those commodities and technologies controlled under U.S. Export Administration Regulations.  It is Motive's policy to require that employees be authorized to receive access to Motive products and technology.  Regarding US-based roles, depending on your role and primary work location, Motive Technologies, Inc. (“Employer”) discloses candidates may be required to execute a non-compete covenant with the Employer. This requirement does not apply to lawyers, interns, or employees working in CA, MN, MT, ND, OK, or where otherwise prohibited by law. Non-compete covenant terms in all other jurisdictions will be subject to the applicable statutory requirements, including but not limited to, procedures, industry related prohibitions, or salary and compensation thresholds. All job postings are for existing vacancies. Please note; some interviews or new-hire training sessions may be held in person at one of our global offices.

jobs.title: Marketing Data Science Manager
jobs.description: To learn the Hiring Ranges for this position, please select your location from the Apply Now dropdown menu. To learn more about our Hiring Range System, please click this link. Why Mozilla? Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.  The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.  About this team and role: In the past few years, Marketing has emerged as a key vector and focus of Firefox’s growth, with Data Science playing an essential role in evaluating Marketing’s impact and developing clear strategies to ensure that success. Marketing Data Science supports Firefox through the standard fare of marketing (ongoing measurement, experimentation/lift testing, adhoc analysis, forecasting/budget optimization), and beyond that as thought leaders at Firefox in translating broad goals into clearly defined objectives and identifying the path towards succeeding in them.  In this role, you will continue to build on the Marketing team’s recent successes as Firefox’s Marketing program continues to expand its footprint throughout the funnel. You’ll look to support this success in owning global data strategy for Firefox Marketing, developing new data capabilities to unlock future business growth, collaborating with Data Science counterparts in other domains domains, and working closely across marketing and adjacent cross-functional teams to translate your team’s work into practical recommendations and enablement that drive Firefox’s growth.  What you’ll do: Set the strategy and roadmap for Marketing Data Science, prioritizing the highest-impact opportunities with key partners. Establish goals and measurement approaches for attribution, ROI, and campaign performance; deliver insights that improve marketing investment and outcomes. Lead and develop the team’s core capabilities across: Performance marketing: budget optimization, causal lift measurement, and conversion-signal testing Brand marketing: measurement planning and assessment of long-term and lower-funnel impact User insights: retention/LTV modeling and audience segmentation Reporting and infrastructure: build self-service dashboards, deliver ad hoc and executive reporting, and develop scalable data models and internal tools that expand our understanding of the acquisition landscape. Bring a forward-looking perspective on advertising, media innovation, and marketing analytics methods. Partner with Data Science leaders to evaluate and responsibly adopt emerging AI tools that improve team workflows and impact. What you’ll bring: 6+ years of marketing data science experience, ideally at a media agency or in-house marketing organization. Proficiency with marketing analytics tools, including Google Analytics and advertising platforms, and familiarity with modeling methods such as MMM, causal lift/synthetic control, saturation modeling, optimization, and Bayesian approaches. Proven experience leading, mentoring, and developing talent, with strong stakeholder management and the ability to prioritize multiple complex workstreams. Strong storytelling and communication skills, with the ability to tailor data-driven insights and recommendations to different audiences.  What you’ll get: Generous performance-based bonus plans to all eligible employees - we share in our success as one team Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute) Quarterly all-company wellness days where everyone takes a pause together Country specific holidays plus a day off for your birthday One-time home office stipend Annual professional development budget Quarterly well-being stipend Considerable paid parental leave Employee referral bonus program Other benefits (life/AD&D, disability, EAP, etc. - varies by country) About Mozilla  Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Join us to work on the Web as the platform and help create more opportunity and innovation for everyone online. Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging Mozilla understands that valuing diverse creative practices and forms of knowledge are crucial to and enrich the company’s core mission.  We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, persons of all sexual orientation s, gender identities, and expressions. We will ensure that qualified individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, as appropriate. Please contact us at hiringaccommodation@mozilla.com to request accommodation. We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race (including hairstyle and texture), religion (including religious grooming and dress practices), gender, gender identity, gender expression, color, national origin, pregnancy, ancestry, domestic partner status, disability, sexual orientation, age, genetic predisposition, medical condition, marital status, citizenship status, military or veteran status, or any other basis covered by applicable laws.  Mozilla will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics or any other unlawful behavior, conduct, or purpose. jobs.title: Global Partner Marketing Programs Manager
jobs.description: Come join the organization that is redefining security for the AI era. As one of the fastest-growing startups ever, we enable teams to secure cloud and AI applications by connecting code, cloud, and runtime into a single shared context. Trusted by security teams all over the world, we have a proven track record of success and a culture that values world-class talent. Not to mention, we're now powered by Google , meaning we offer our customers an AI-powered platform that harnesses Google’s Threat Intelligence and Security Operations to better detect, prevent, and respond to threats across all environments, allowing for further innovation. Our Wizards from all over the globe work together to protect the infrastructure of our customers, including over 65% of the Fortune 100, who trust us to scan and secure over 230 billion files daily. We’re honored to be a leading player in a massive and growing market, and we continue to look for exceptional Wizards who are eager to make a significant impact on our team. At Wiz, you’ll have the freedom to think creatively, dream big, and use your full range of skills to contribute to our momentous growth. Come join our team and help us create secure cloud environments that allow even the best companies to move faster, all while having some fun! Minimum qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, or a related field. 8+ years of experience in B2B partner/channel marketing or GTM demand generation experience. Proven track record of designing multi-channel demand generation campaigns and account-based marketing strategies across a partner ecosystem. Deep understanding of channel ecosystem sales models, pipeline tracking, and measuring attribution. Solid understanding of the partner ecosystem landscape (Channel, GSIs, MSPs, Cloud Marketplaces/CSPs). Ability to align global strategy with regional execution teams to ensure smooth campaign rollout and lead follow-up. Strong communication and interpersonal skills to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced environment. Preferred qualifications MBA Experience in a high-growth B2B SaaS/Enterprise technology landscape, with a background in cybersecurity or cloud security. Proficiency in Salesforce, Looker, and marketing automation to track full-funnel partner impact (Analytical Rigor). Ability to turn complex business goals into actionable marketing blueprints for a regional team (Strategic Architect). Experience building processes that allow a marketing function to stay "lock-step" with rapid sales growth (Operational Scaling). Ability to manage the competing priorities and "noise" between Sales, Partners, and Corporate stakeholders (Conflict Resolution). jobs.description: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. The Opportunity  Grafana's Demand Generation team creates and accelerates pipeline across the full customer journey. We run a modern, AI-forward operation: lifecycle email programs driven by an AI engine, territory-level buying signals surfaced directly to sales leaders, and agentic workflows that handle work that used to take teams of specialists. Our webinar program is one of the highest-leverage things we run: technical, practitioner-first sessions on a weekly cadence across AMER, EMEA, APAC and LATAM, putting the product in front of the people who would actually use it. Hands-on sessions, not sales pitches. We're hiring a Webinar Program Manager to own it. This is a specialist seat, not a generalist one. You'll inherit an established program with a documented process and a full handover from the person who built it, and you'll own the operating rhythm from there: the calendar, the presenters, the build and promotion of every session, the follow-up, and the reporting. This is not a "run the playbook" role. Sessions run in parallel at a pace no one could manage by hand, so the way to raise quality is to keep automating the mechanics. We expect this person to build with AI as a default and treat automation as a first-class deliverable, not a side project. You'd be joining a demand gen team that is genuinely rebuilding how the function works, where AI agents run real production programs and the people on the team design the machine rather than turn the crank. The webinar program already produces, and much of the pipeline it touches starts with a session rather than a seller. You're not here to prove webinars matter. You're here to make each one produce more with less manual work behind it. What You'll Be Doing Own the webinar calendar end to end. Presenter booking, registration pages, campaign setup, promotion, live delivery, follow-up, and the flip to on-demand, across multiple regions and time zones. Keep sessions practitioner-first. Brief technical presenters, shape the outline, and keep a session useful to the audience that registered for it. Bring data to topic planning. Use past performance and downstream pipeline quality to recommend what we run and what we retire, and lock the plan with demand gen and product marketing each quarter. Automate the production line. Extend the automation behind session setup and promotion, and keep pushing into the parts of the process a person shouldn't be doing by hand, including repurposing recordings into other content. Report on what happens after the session. Registrations are the input. Connect sessions to product adoption and pipeline, report it honestly, and flag what isn't producing. Grow the program's reach. Expand into additional languages and formats where the numbers justify it. What Makes You a Great Fit 4+ years in demand generation, event marketing, or lifecycle marketing at a B2B software company (open source or developer-focused a plus). Hands-on ownership of a recurring webinar or virtual event calendar across multiple regions. A cadence you were accountable for hitting, not a handful of one-off sessions. Hands-on with a webinar platform (ON24, Zoom Webinars, Contrast, Goldcast or similar) and the plumbing behind it: CRM campaigns, registration sync, attendance data, follow-up triggers. Comfortable working with technical presenters. You can brief an engineer or solutions architect and hold the line on what the audience came for. Hands-on with AI in your actual work: you've built automations or agentic workflows (or are visibly on that path), and you think about AI as leverage, not a threat or a buzzword. Comfortable with data: you can pull your own numbers, sanity-check them, and build a program readout a VP would trust. Strong program management fundamentals. Twenty-plus moving pieces at once is a logistics job before it's a marketing job, and you ship on time without needing a coordinator. Bonus Points For Content repurposing at scale: clips, blog, social, on-demand libraries. Localized program experience, and a view on when translation earns its cost. Familiarity with the observability, monitoring or open source ecosystem. Customer.io, Salesforce and a modern data stack (BigQuery or similar). Experience with product-led motions alongside sales-led ones. jobs.title: Director, Marketing Analytics
jobs.description: About The Princeton Review   The Princeton Review is a leading tutoring, test prep, and college admission services company. Every year, it helps millions of college- and graduate school–bound students achieve their education and career goals through online and in-person courses delivered by a network of more than 4,000 teachers and tutors, online resources, and its more than 150 print and digital books published by Penguin Random House. The company’s  Tutor.com  brand is one of the largest online tutoring services in the U.S. It comprises a community of thousands of tutors who have delivered more than 22 million one-to-one tutoring sessions. The Princeton Review is headquartered in New York, NY. Follow the company on  LinkedIn ,  YouTube  and  Instagram .    About the Position    We're looking for a strategic analytics leader to own revenue metrics across the customer lifecycle—from acquisition through retention. This role is perfect for someone who loves understanding the complete customer journey, optimizing unit economics, and empowering teams with data-driven insights that directly impact company growth.   You'll report to our VP of Consumer Revenue and partner with marketing, sales, and customer success teams. You’ll have insights to lead cross-functional analytics that drive customer acquisition, conversion, and retention. This leader will own marketing analytics alongside sales funnel insights and customer lifetime value metrics. You'll translate complex data into actionable insights that directly impact our revenue and unit economics. You'll blend marketing analytics rigor with sales funnel insights and customer lifetime value optimization.   What You'll Do   Analyze the Complete Revenue Picture   Track customer acquisition cost (CAC) and lifetime value (LTV) by channel   Understand which marketing channels drive the highest-quality leads and best ROI   Analyze sales funnel metrics and identify conversion bottlenecks   Identify retention drivers and churn patterns to improve LTV   Build Revenue Analytics Infrastructure   Own marketing analytics, sales funnel reporting, and customer retention dashboards   Manage the marketing tech stack and integrations (Braze, Salesforce, tracking)   Establish consistent revenue metrics across all functions   Create executive reporting that enables fast, confident decisions   Drive Revenue Insights & Optimization   Identify 5+ analytics-driven initiatives to improve unit economics   Calculate payback periods and ROI by channel   Recommend pricing, positioning, and retention strategies informed by data   Partner with marketing, sales, and customer success on data-driven initiatives   Lead a High-Performing Analytics Team   Hire and develop 3–5 analytics professionals   Create career development paths and establish best practices   Align analytics across revenue functions   Who You Are     You have 7–10+ years of analytics experience, with proven expertise in both marketing analytics and revenue metrics (CAC, LTV, retention). You're comfortable diving deep into data while keeping business impact front and center. You thrive in cross-functional environments and love translating data into decisions.   Key Skills & Experience:   Strong SQL and data visualization (Tableau, Looker, PowerBI)   Deep knowledge of marketing funnel, attribution, and channel analytics   Expertise in SaaS metrics (CAC, LTV, cohort retention, churn, payback period)   Hands-on experience with marketing technology (Braze, Salesforce, Google Tag Manager)   Familiarity with sales funnel and CRM analytics   Ability to analyze complex customer journeys across channels and touchpoints   Proven ability to partner with non-technical stakeholders and drive adoption   Leadership experience managing analytics teams   Nice to Have:   SaaS or subscription business background   Experience with customer segmentation and cohort analysis   Predictive analytics or forecasting experience   Growth marketing or experimentation knowledge   Data warehouse experience (Snowflake, Redshift, etc.)   What Success Looks Like   In your first year, you'll establish trusted revenue dashboards that marketing, sales, and customer success teams rely on daily. You'll identify and help implement 5+ initiatives that improve unit economics—whether through better channel targeting, faster sales cycles, or improved retention. You'll reduce manual reporting time by 50%, freeing up your team to focus on analysis and insight. Most importantly, you'll be known as the leader who made data central to every revenue decision.   Why You'll Love This Role   Revenue Impact: Your work directly influences company growth and profitability Hybrid Scope: Analyze the complete customer lifecycle, not just one function   Cross-Functional Leadership: Partner with marketing, sales, product, and finance leaders   Business Criticality: Analytics inform every major decision across revenue functions   Team Building: Hire and develop a diverse analytics team   Remote Flexibility: Work from anywhere in the US with a fully distributed team     The Princeton Review and Tutor.com offer a competitive salary which commensurates with experience and skills.  US Pay Range $150,000 — $175,000 USD The Princeton Review is an equal employment opportunity employer. As the category leader in Autonomous Cloud and AI Infrastructure Resource Management, we're trusted by leading enterprises including Adobe, Wiz, Epic Games, Northwestern Mutual, Coinbase, DocuSign, and Fortune 100 companies to autonomously manage their most critical production environments.  Backed by Insight Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and other leading VCs with over $210M in funding, ScaleOps is the leading player in a massive and growing market. We are building the autonomous infrastructure management platform that will power the next decade of enterprise compute. What You'll Be Doing We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager to own how we position, launch, and communicate our products to the market, and to build ScaleOps' presence with the analyst community. This person will lead messaging, competitive intelligence, analyst relations, enablement content, and go-to-market strategies that resonate with technical buyers, from DevOps engineers to infrastructure-focused executives. Define and continuously refine messaging and positioning for ScaleOps products and features, ensuring clarity and consistency across all channels and audiences. Lead end-to-end GTM strategy for product launches, from naming and positioning through enablement, campaign orchestration, and post-launch measurement. Own analyst relations completely, including managing relationships with firms like Gartner and Forrester, coordinating briefings and inquiries, responding to research requests, and ensuring ScaleOps is accurately and favorably represented in relevant reports and evaluations. Conduct win/loss interviews, competitive analysis, and customer research to sharpen positioning and keep the team ahead of market shifts. Develop high-quality sales and customer-facing materials, including pitch decks, one-pagers, battlecards, and technical explainers. Collaborate closely with Product, Sales, DevRel, and Content to ensure a unified narrative across the funnel. Act as the voice of the market in roadmap planning, pricing discussions, and strategic initiatives. Identify opportunities to incorporate AI tools into content creation, competitive research, and campaign workflows to increase speed and quality of output. Track and report on PMM impact across pipeline influence, win rates, analyst positioning, and content usage. What You'll Bring 4–6 years of B2B SaaS product marketing experience; devtools, infrastructure, or cloud experience is a strong plus. Proven ability to translate complex technical concepts into strategic business narratives that resonate with both technical and executive audiences. Exceptional writing and storytelling skills, with a developer-savvy tone and strong instincts for what lands with infrastructure buyers. Experience owning product launches end-to-end, with a track record of driving measurable pipeline impact. Hands-on experience managing analyst relations, including briefings, inquiries, and report participation with major firms. Comfortable operating in a high-growth startup environment with a high degree of autonomy. Deep knowledge of Kubernetes, cloud cost, or the DevOps ecosystem is required. Curiosity about AI tools and how they can accelerate research, content, and go-to-market execution.
