jobs.title: Digital Marketing Manager - Americas
jobs.description: About Appspace: At Appspace, we’re passionate about creating better work experiences for people everywhere, and we’re looking for people that feel the same way. Our global office locations and flexible work culture help you work wherever and however you’re at your best. Plus, we take the time to help you enjoy your work, build lasting connections, and grow your role. Join the Appspace team and be a part of a culture that’s helping people everywhere love where they work. Your Role as a Digital Marketing Manager: We’re looking for a performance-obsessed Digital Marketing Manager to own and scale Appspace’s paid media engine. Paid media is the primary mandate of this role—you will control significant advertising budgets across search, social, and display channels, and be held accountable for pipeline contribution and ROAS. Beyond paid, you’ll help optimize our website for conversion and AI-engine discoverability, and partner cross-functionally to ensure every dollar of digital spend is tied directly to revenue outcomes. This is not a generalist role. The right candidate lives in campaign dashboards, obsesses over cost-per-opportunity, and knows how to scale what’s working while ruthlessly cutting what isn’t. A Day in the Life of a Digital Marketing Manager: Own and Optimize Paid Media Programs  Paid media performance is the core metric by which this role is measured. You will: Manage and allocate multi-channel paid media budgets across Google Ads (Search, Display, P-Max), LinkedIn Campaign Manager, 6sense, and Meta Ads—continuously rebalancing based on pipeline contribution and cost-per-opportunity. Build and maintain always-on advertising programs alongside point-in-time campaign bursts, ensuring consistent pipeline coverage throughout the fiscal year. Develop quarterly paid media plans grounded in buyer persona research, intent data, and competitive analysis; translate strategy into channel-specific execution plans with clear KPIs. Define and own paid media KPIs: CTR, CPC, CPL, cost-per-MQL, cost-per-opportunity, ROAS, and pipeline-influenced revenue. Report weekly to senior leadership. Run structured A/B tests on ad copy, creative, audience segments, bidding strategies, and landing pages; document results and scale winners systematically. Design and test ad creative and copy by leveraging AI generation tools alongside content and design teams—using performance data to drive the next iteration of brand assets. Leverage B2B intent data and account-intelligence platforms (e.g., 6sense, Demandbase, Bombora) to build targeted ABM ad campaigns aligned with Sales outbound targets. Stay current with platform algorithm changes (Google’s AI-driven bidding, LinkedIn audience expansion, Meta Advantage+) and adapt strategies proactively. Optimize Website Performance Measure and monitor the Appspace website’s health, performance, and conversion rates; share regular dashboards with marketing leadership and stakeholders. Optimize web content, layout, structure, and UX for both human conversions (CRO) and AI-engine discoverability (SEO/AEO), ensuring Appspace surfaces across both traditional search and AI-powered discovery. Manage and coordinate with Appspace’s external SEO agency—set deliverables, hold the agency accountable to results, and integrate SEO insights into paid media and content strategies. Implement and maintain website tracking through Google Tag Manager. Collaborate Across the Marketing & Revenue Team Feed paid media performance data, search intent trends, and AI-discovery insights back into the content engine—partnering with creative, copywriting, and content teams so messaging continually evolves based on real-time market signals. Work hand-in-hand with Revenue Operations to manage multi-touch attribution models, ensuring all digital spend is mapped to pipeline velocity and closed-won revenue. Support integrated campaigns by handling all paid advertising components: planning, audience building, ad construction, trafficking, and measurement. Contribute to quarterly and annual marketing planning by providing paid media performance data and forward-looking budget recommendations. What You'll Need: Paid Media Expertise (Required): 5+ years managing substantial B2B SaaS paid media budgets with demonstrable results—specific experience driving pipeline from Google Ads, LinkedIn, and Meta is essential. Please be prepared to share performance results. AI-Augmented Execution: Hands-on use of AI-driven marketing workflows—ad copy generation, audience modeling, bid optimization, and creative testing at scale. Platform Mastery: Expert-level command of Google Ads, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Meta Ads Manager, GA4, GTM and SFDC reporting. ABM & Intent Data: Practical experience using B2B intent platforms (6sense, Demandbase, or equivalent) to build targeted account-based campaigns in close partnership with Sales. Analytical Rigor: Ability to move beyond surface-level reporting—interpret multi-touch attribution, journey-aware bidding signals, and predictive analytics to make budget decisions with confidence. Web & CRO Fluency: Solid understanding of CMS management, landing page builders (e.g., Unbounce, Webflow), and conversion rate optimization best practices. Revenue Mindset: Comfortable tying digital spend directly to pipeline and closed-won revenue; you speak the language of Sales and RevOps, not just marketing. Adaptability: A bias for action and experimentation in a fast-changing landscape where AI platforms and buyer behaviors shift quickly. For all our Canadian based team members, we offer a variety of benefits from competitive salaries, medical, dental and vision coverage, ongoing training opportunities, gym membership reimbursement, mental health resources, and a fully paid maternity and parental leave program.  Generous PTO 5 additional days off for training  Flexible work schedules Remote work opportunities Appspace Quiet Fridays (No non-essential internal meetings scheduled) Paid company holidays   Disclaimer: Appspace is committed to equitable compensation practices and complies with all applicable local, state, and federal regulations. For jurisdictions that require pay scale disclosure, a general compensation range may be provided during the initial stages of the interview process. Final compensation will be based on multiple factors including experience, skills, certifications, and overall fit for the role. If you are located in a jurisdiction with specific pay transparency requirements, we will be happy to discuss the relevant range during your application process.

jobs.title: Sr. Solutions Marketing Manager
jobs.description: Intelligence Center X is Siemens' platform for the agentic enterprise The next wave of enterprise software isn't about writing more code — it's about giving organizations the tools to combine trusted data, AI, and applications into systems that can reason and act on their own. Intelligence Center X delivers that today, through five capabilities — an Enterprise Knowledge Graph, AI/ML, agentic application development, orchestration, and governance — that together move enterprises from static software to intelligent, autonomous systems. For the customers we serve, that shift shows up in very concrete ways: engineers and data leaders who can finally find and trust the data buried across decades of enterprise systems; teams that go from idea to working application in days instead of quarters; and AI initiatives that move out of pilot purgatory and into production because the underlying data and governance can actually support them. Whether you're building this platform, proving its value to customers, or bringing it to market through our partner ecosystem, your work directly drives those outcomes for some of the most complex organizations in the world. This is one of the most ambitious enterprise AI platforms in the market — built on decades of deep domain expertise across industries as varied as manufacturing, banking, insurance, financial services, and healthcare, and already running in production at real scale for organizations with some of the most demanding data and compliance requirements in the world. If you want to work at the intersection of enterprise AI, knowledge graphs, and agentic applications — with real customers and real production stakes, across nearly every major industry — this is where that work is happening. Job Description Role Overview Siemens Digital Industries Software is looking for a Senior Solutions Marketing Manager to join the specialized Growth team focused on Intelligence Center X, Siemens' agentic enterprise system and Mendix. Reporting to the Senior Director of Solutions Marketing, this role is responsible for developing compelling solution narratives that connect Intelligence Center X and its portfolio of products to the business challenges, priorities, and opportunities facing enterprise customers. Working across Product Marketing, Sales, Industry teams, Campaigns, and Field Marketing, you will translate the core platform story into customer-centric messaging, industry solution plays, and sales-ready content that accelerates pipeline and supports strategic growth initiatives. This is a highly collaborative role for a strategic marketer who enjoys simplifying complex technologies into compelling business stories that resonate with executive buyers and technical decision-makers. Key Responsibilities Solution Messaging and Positioning Develop differentiated solution messaging and positioning for Intelligence Center X and Mendix across priority industries and use cases. Translate platform capabilities into customer-focused narratives that clearly articulate business outcomes and value. Create messaging frameworks tailored to key buying personas, including CIOs, business leaders, data and AI teams, and application developers. Ensure solution messaging aligns with the overarching Intelligence Center X and Mendix narrative while addressing industry-specific priorities. Industry and Use Case Development Build solution stories around strategic business challenges, emerging AI opportunities, and digital transformation initiatives. Develop industry-specific messaging for aerospace and defence, automotive, heavy equipment and industrial machinery and other priority industries. Partner with industry experts to ensure messaging reflects market trends, customer needs, and competitive differentiation. Identify new solution opportunities and emerging market themes to strengthen Siemens' market position. Go-to-Market Enablement Create solution briefs, messaging guides, presentations, playbooks, sales tools, and customer-facing assets. Support product launches, campaigns, webinars, events, analyst engagements, and executive presentations. Enable sales and field teams with messaging that helps position Intelligence Center X and Mendix against customer priorities and competitive alternatives. Support strategic customer opportunities by tailoring solution narratives for priority accounts. Cross-functional Collaboration Partner closely with Product Marketing to ensure solution messaging accurately reflects platform capabilities and roadmap priorities. Work with Campaigns and Field Marketing to develop integrated go-to-market programs and industry campaigns. Collaborate with Brand and Communications to reinforce strategic messaging themes and thought leadership. Gather customer, sales, and market feedback to continuously refine messaging and identify new opportunities. Market Intelligence Monitor competitive positioning, market trends, and customer challenges across target industries. Bring market insights into messaging development and go-to-market planning. Identify whitespace opportunities where Intelligence Center X can create differentiated customer value. Qualifications Required 6–10 years of experience in Solutions Marketing, Product Marketing, Industry Marketing, or Go-to-Market roles within enterprise software or B2B SaaS. Experience developing solution messaging for AI, analytics, cloud platforms, application development, or enterprise technology. Strong understanding of enterprise buying journeys and complex solution selling. Experience creating sales enablement content and customer-facing messaging. Excellent written, presentation, and storytelling skills with the ability to simplify complex technologies. Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills across product, sales, marketing, and leadership teams. Ability to work effectively within a global, matrixed organization. Preferred Experience marketing AI, machine learning, low-code platforms, data platforms, or digital transformation technologies. Knowledge of industrial manufacturing, financial services, public sector, life sciences, energy, or other enterprise industries. Experience supporting analyst relations, executive thought leadership, or strategic customer engagements. Success Measures In this role, you will: Deliver compelling solution narratives that increase customer engagement and strengthen Intelligence Center X's market positioning. Enable sales teams with messaging and content that supports pipeline generation and deal acceleration. Produce high-impact industry messaging that aligns with customer priorities and strategic growth markets. Improve consistency of solution storytelling across campaigns, product launches, and field execution. Build trusted relationships across Product, Sales, Industry Marketing, and Campaign teams as the go-to expert for solution messaging. Compensation and Benefits The pay range for this position is $102,500 - $184,500 annually. The actual wage offered may be lower or higher within this range depending on budget and candidate experience, knowledge, skills, qualifications, and premium geographic location. In addition to the base salary, Siemens offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) plan with company match, paid time off, and professional development opportunities.

jobs.description: Silverback Strategies is a performance marketing agency built to help marketers grow and capitalize on change. Ad Age, Inc Magazine, The Washington Post, The Washingtonian, and The Washington Business Journal have recognized Silverback as one of the best places to work. We hire the best and help them get better. Silverbackers are supported, challenged and inspired by their peers. Regardless of title or tenure, every Silverbacker plays a role in helping our agency get better. This is a place where you can make a difference. Silverback’s next SEO Manager will serve as a premier subject matter expert in all things related to SEO & Organic Search. You will develop and manage a portfolio of 4-6 SEO accounts while building great client relationships and managing projects & deliverables. You’ll bring a scrappy & tenacious attitude to your work, diving headfirst into the “new frontier” of organic search by pushing the boundaries of AI search testing. You’ll also flex best-in-class data analysis chops to break down performance metrics and directly impact the success of our clients’ businesses. Here’s what we expect from our SEO Manager: Strategic Chops: Responsible for driving and executing the strategy, innovation and performance of multiple client SEO strategies. AI & LLM Expertise: Hands-on experience with Generative AI and LLMs, including their influence on search behavior and the ability to implement optimized strategies for these engines. Analytical Skills: Fluently leverage tools such as Google Analytics, Google Search Console, SEMrush, Ahrefs, and other SEO platforms, with a demonstrated ability to translate complex data into actionable insights. Client-Facing: Lead recurring status and reporting calls & serve as assigned clients’ primary point of contact with Silverback for all things SEO. Clearly communicate complex SEO strategy and execution details to clients in a digestible, jargon-free manner. Client Management: Act as a trusted advisor & consultant to clients — an extension of their marketing team — to build long-lasting client relationships. Tactical Execution: Translate channel strategy to time-bound, tactical roadmaps. Build and maintain structured content systems, including topic clusters, pillar pages, internal links, and supporting schema. Prioritize performance-based initiatives and drive authoritative content at scale. Innovation: Research emerging trends in search and AI technologies to refine strategies and implement innovative best practices. Data Analysis: Review performance data to identify trends, measure the impact of initiatives and build actionable strategies. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with internal teammates across measurement, paid media, and creative to bring strategies to life. Agency Background: You’ve previously “done the work” at another performance marketing agency, and know what it takes to deliver results Years of Experience: We’re seeking candidates with at LEAST 2 years of agency experience; 3 years of overall relevant marketing/SEO experience is required, 5+ years preferred. Client-Facing Comfortability: This role is not a good fit for someone who doesn’t want to talk directly to clients. You must be comfortable building rapport, establishing expertise / credibility, and serving as the face of the SEO engagement with your assigned clients. AI Search Testing & Optimization: You have hands-on experience optimizing for AI search (not theoretical; actual tests). You don’t have all the answers — nobody does! — but you’re excited to test, experiment, and figure it out. Business Acumen: Being able to build & execute SEO strategies across multiple industries is crucial, but your ability to tie SEO wins to a measurable impact on the clients’ business, bottom line, etc is what will make you a superstar. Content Experience: You’re an expert at driving content strategy based on audience, keyword and competitor research. You have a strong ability to craft content briefs to provide to content teams for production. Tools/Platforms: You’re a pro with common SEO tools & platforms such as Google Search Console, Google Analytics, SEMrush, AHRefs, and Screaming Frog. “Get Sh*t Done” Mentality: You’d rather take a big swing and miss than sit around twiddling your thumbs. You’re energized by & thrive in an environment where no two days are the same, and results are king. Adaptability & Growth: Feedback fuels you. You lean into change, sharpen your skills, and push yourself and your team to get better every day. Project & Time Management: You run a clean calendar and keep priorities straight. Competing demands don’t throw you. Silverback isn’t for everybody. If you’re an A player, you will get paid more, learn more and grow faster with support from a smart and fun team. If you’re a B player, you will be miserable. Make an impact: We’re a small agency. Everybody has the opportunity to drive change and impact. Get paid: We hire the best and pay them generously. Do cool sh*t: From media to SEO to measurement, learn the cutting edge of what works. Unlimited PTO Comprehensive health, dental, and vision plans Monthly Team Events and a fun, casual, inclusive company culture Company-paid ClassPass membership 12 weeks of Paid Parental Leave Summer Fridays 401(k) with Employer Match We’re a fully remote agency with employees working across the continental United States. At Silverback, you'll be part of a remote work culture that emphasizes smooth, productive online communication. We at Silverback pride ourselves on being an extremely tight-knit team. We boast an unparalleled culture of collaboration, empathy, and a truly "work hard, play hard" mentality. Ad Age, Inc. Magazine and The Washington Post have named Silverback one of the best places to work in the Country and our CEO is a DIGIDAY Top Boss. Apply today & discover for yourself what makes Silverback Strategies such a special place to work. We can't wait to hear from you! Silverback Strategies is an equal opportunity employer. If you believe you meet the qualifications for the position, then we invite you to apply. We celebrate the free flow of conversation, ideas and opinions at Silverback, but actions such as bullying, discrimination, harassment or retaliation of any kind are strictly prohibited in our workplace. We are committed to providing a safe, open and accommodating environment that allows all of our team members to thrive. Employment decisions are made without regard to age, color, disability, family, genetic information, origin, race, religion, sex. For more information, we invite you to visit eeoc.gov.

Curious and adaptable, with a willingness to embrace AI and emerging marketing technologies to improve productivity, campaign performance, and customer experiences. We pride ourselves on providing Inventory Management and Supply Chain software to help medium-large product businesses thrive in a highly competitive, digital world. While Adobe Experience Cloud represents a dominant ecosystem within the Bounteous practice, this role is intentionally multi-platform. The Director is expected to bring strong Adobe expertise alongside working knowledge of complementary marketing technology platforms and patterns, including CRM, CDP, marketing automation, analytics, and personalization technologies. The role spans both B2B and B2C use cases, with an emphasis on data-driven orchestration, lifecycle marketing, and measurable business outcomes rather than CMS- or DAM-centric implementations. This position serves as a bridge between sales and delivery, acting as a trusted advisor to clients and platform partners while also setting delivery teams up for success. Architect solutions spanning CDP, marketing automation, journey orchestration, analytics, personalization, and CRM integrations. Translate business objectives into platform architectures, data models, integration patterns, and activation strategies. Maintain awareness of evolving MarTech capabilities, ecosystem trends, and emerging technologies. Maintain an active billable role across client engagements, contributing directly to discovery, solutioning, and delivery oversight. Lead client workshops, discovery sessions, demos, and executive presentations. Partner with delivery teams to ensure solutions are implemented in alignment with architectural intent and best practices. Support escalation, troubleshooting, and course correction on complex marketing technology programs. Pre-Sales, Growth, and Partnerships Partner with client service and business development teams to support pursuits, pitches, and account expansion. Support pre-sales solutioning through consultative discovery, estimates, and solution narratives. Identify opportunities to create packaged offerings, accelerators, and repeatable solution patterns Collaborate with platform partners, including Adobe and other MarTech vendors, on roadmap awareness, co-innovation, and solution alignment. Governance, Enablement, and Thought Leadership Guide clients in establishing marketing technology governance models, operating models, and Centers of Excellence. Define best practices for data stewardship, consent management, orchestration, and measurement. Provide thought leadership in the marketing technology space, helping position Bounteous as a trusted partner for enterprise MarTech transformation. Mentor architects and senior practitioners, contributing to internal enablement, frameworks, and best-practice playbooks. Preferred Qualifications 10 or more years of experience designing, architecting, and delivering marketing technology solutions. 3 or more years of experience in a digital-first, global delivery agency or consultancy. Deep experience with Adobe Experience Cloud, including platforms such as Adobe Experience Platform, Journey Optimizer, Marketo Engage, Customer Journey Analytics, and related tools. Working knowledge of non-Adobe MarTech platforms such as Salesforce, Braze, Iterable, or similar, with the ability to architect across ecosystems. Strong understanding of CRM, CDP, analytics, identity, and data integration patterns. Proven ability to operate in a consultative, client-facing role while maintaining billable delivery responsibilities. Demonstrated success translating complex technical ecosystems into measurable business outcomes. Excellent executive communication skills with the ability to influence both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Marketing, or a related field, or equivalent experience. jobs.title: Content Marketing Manager, Professional Learning & Growth
jobs.description: At Colibri Group, culture is at the heart of everything we do. Our values Love, Joy, Boldness, Teamwork, and Curiosity, guide how we work together, support our customers, and make a difference in the communities we serve. Colibri Group is a leader in online professional education, serving more than one million learners each year across a family of trusted education brands. Moreland University, part of our Teacher Education Ecosystem, supports educators around the world through innovative pathways into the teaching profession and continued professional growth. Come Build What’s Next We’re looking for a Content Marketing Manager – Professional Learning to help build and scale Moreland University’s professional learning offering for educators. This is an individual contributor role with meaningful ownership over a new area of growth for Moreland. We’ve spent the last several years testing professional learning experiences with educators and have seen strong interest and demand. Now, we’re ready to turn that momentum into a scalable portfolio of on-demand courses, learning journeys, live experiences, and ultimately new subscription-based offerings. You’ll own the professional learning go-to-market calendar and help move new offerings from idea through launch — partnering closely with faculty and subject matter experts who develop the curriculum while you provide project leadership, audience insight, editorial guidance, and marketing expertise. We’re looking for a content marketer first: someone who can write, position, launch, and promote educational offerings while keeping multiple projects, stakeholders, and deadlines moving forward. Experience working with educators, teachers, EdTech, professional learning, or another teacher-facing audience will be especially valuable. You should be equally comfortable writing a landing page, building a launch calendar, guiding a subject matter expert through a project, reviewing learning materials for quality and audience fit, and looking at engagement data to determine what we should build next. What You’ll Do Own the professional learning portfolio and launch calendar, helping prioritize, plan, and bring new on-demand courses, learning journeys, certificates, microcredentials, webinars, and other educator experiences to market Lead projects from concept through launch, coordinating faculty, subject matter experts, creative partners, and cross-functional teams while keeping timelines, deliverables, and launch readiness on track Create compelling short and long form marketing content including landing pages, course titles and descriptions, email campaigns, blog content, promotional messaging, participant communications, and sales enablement materials Build and execute go-to-market strategies that drive awareness, registrations, subscriptions, repeat engagement, and long-term growth across Moreland’s professional learning portfolio Use learner feedback, participation data, market insights, and performance metrics to improve existing offerings, identify new opportunities, and help scale professional learning into a meaningful new growth channel for Moreland What You’ll Bring 4+ years of experience in content marketing or a closely related role, ideally within education, EdTech, professional learning, online learning, or another educator-facing environment Direct experience creating marketing content and bringing programs, educational offerings, digital content, courses, events, or similar products to market not simply supporting content after launch Strong writing and editorial skills across short- and long-form content, with the ability to translate educational concepts into clear, engaging messaging for teachers and other educator audiences Demonstrated ability to manage complex, cross-functional projects from idea through execution, including coordinating subject matter experts or other partners who own specialized content A combination of creative thinking, organization, audience empathy, and commercial awareness, with the ability to use performance insights to improve engagement and inform what gets built next A bachelor’s degree is required. A degree in marketing, communications, education, instructional design, English, journalism, or a related field is preferred. Experience as an educator, former teacher, or in another teacher-facing role is a meaningful plus. Experience with subscription-based products, learning platforms, digital content libraries, or professional learning portfolios is also valuable. Tools, Platforms, and Methodologies You May Use Experience with every tool or platform below is not required. We care most about your ability to create excellent content, manage work effectively, collaborate with experts, and use technology thoughtfully to improve how you work. Content management and email marketing platforms Project management and collaboration tools Learning management or digital learning platforms Analytics and performance-reporting tools AI-assisted content and productivity tools, including Claude or similar platforms We believe AI can be a powerful partner in the creative and operational process. You’ll be encouraged to use it thoughtfully to improve efficiency, support content development, and strengthen the learner experience while maintaining high standards for originality, quality, and brand integrity. Why You’ll Love Working Here Build something new: You’ll help take a successful professional learning concept and turn it into a scalable offering for educators Own meaningful work: This is not a small piece of someone else’s strategy, you’ll have significant ownership over the professional learning portfolio and how it goes to market Work with people who know education: You’ll partner with an experienced faculty community and a strong, established content marketing team Combine creativity with strategy: You’ll get to write and create while also shaping launches, managing projects, and influencing what we build next See the impact: Your work will directly influence how educators discover, engage with, and continue learning through Moreland University Join a mission driven organization where your creativity, judgment, and understanding of educators can have a visible impact We Encourage You to Apply You may not check every preferred box, and that’s okay! We’d especially love to hear from candidates coming from content marketing, education marketing, EdTech, professional learning, continuing education, teacher-facing organizations, or digital learning businesses. Former educators who have since built strong professional experience in marketing and content are also encouraged to apply. However, this role does require strong hands-on content marketing experience, demonstrated project ownership, and the ability to develop marketing content that brings an offering to market. If your recent experience has primarily focused on social media content creation, influencer content, organic social, or curriculum/instructional design without meaningful marketing ownership, this role may not be the right match. If you love writing, understand educators, enjoy bringing ideas to life, and get excited by the opportunity to build a new professional learning offering from the ground up, we’d love to hear from you. What You Can Expect From Our Hiring Process We want our interview process to give you a clear picture of the role, the team, and what it’s like to work at Colibri while giving us the opportunity to understand your experience, how you approach your work, and what you’re looking for next. And yes, a real person reviews your application!! We do not use AI to screen, evaluate, or make decisions on applications. Every application is reviewed by a member of our Talent Acquisition team because we believe and feel your experience deserves a thoughtful, human consideration. Application deadline: 10/16/26 1. Recruiter Conversation An introductory conversation with a member of our Talent Acquisition team to learn more about your experience, career goals, and interest in Colibri. We’ll also share more about the role, team, compensation, and what to expect throughout the process. 2. Hiring Manager Conversation A structured conversation with the Sr. Director of Marketing focused on examples from your experience, your approach to content and project ownership, and the priorities and challenges this person will own. 3. Team & Cross-Functional Conversations You’ll meet with key marketing and cross-functional partners to explore the skills and experiences most relevant to the position while learning more about how the Teacher Education Ecosystem works together. Our goal is to keep the process streamlined, thoughtful, respectful, and transparent. Our Talent Acquisition team will keep you informed about next steps and timing throughout the process. Our Commitment to Inclusion Colibri Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels welcome, respected, and empowered to do their best work. We encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds, experiences, and career paths to apply.

Once all interviews are complete, the manager will be in touch with a final decision. jobs.title: Responsable du marketing produit | Produc Marketing Lead
jobs.description: ValPay builds embedded payments for software companies. Our PayFac-as-a-Service model lets ISVs offer payments to their merchants under their own brand, while we handle underwriting, compliance, and risk. Our partners serve healthcare, legal, hospitality, professional services, and other vertical markets. Launching a payments product is the easy part. The value is created when ISV partners go live, their merchants enroll, and transactions flow. We’re hiring a product marketing Lead whose success is measured by adoption: how quickly and how deeply partners and merchants use our products. You’ll own positioning, launches, and lifecycle marketing across our vertical markets and across North America, Europe, and APAC. You’ll report to the CEO and work closely with product, sales, partnerships, the ISV channel team, and operations. AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research, draft, analyze, and automate. You’re responsible for the quality of the result. What we value Sound judgment and attention to detail. Measuring success by what customers do, not by what we shipped. Taking responsibility and finishing work without being chased. Understanding how the business makes money and caring about results. The honesty to say when something isn’t working, including your own work. What you’ll do Drive partner and merchant adoption: You’ll own the adoption journey end to end: signature, integration, go-live, first transaction, merchant enrollment, and expansion. The hardest gap is between “integrated” and “actively transacting,” and you’ll be the person who finds out where partners and merchants stall and designs programs to close it. That means lifecycle campaigns, onboarding content, and activation playbooks for two audiences at once: the ISV partner and the merchants who use their software. With the ISV channel team, you’ll run co-marketing and merchant-enrollment campaigns that lift penetration within each partner’s customer base. Measure adoption and act on it: You’ll build and maintain the adoption dashboard: activation rate, time to first transaction, attach and penetration rate, volume per merchant, feature adoption, and cohort retention. You’ll use that data to segment partners and merchants, flag at-risk accounts, and surface expansion opportunities, then take what you find to the teams who can act on it. Own positioning and messaging: You’ll develop the positioning, value propositions, and messaging for each product and vertical, and for new verticals and markets as we enter them. A central part of this is explaining clearly how our embedded payments offering differs from horizontal PayFacs, processors, and ISOs. You’ll translate technical capabilities into the outcomes ISVs and merchants care about: revenue share, retention, cleaner reconciliation, and faster onboarding. Run launches built around activation: You’ll lead launch plans for new products, features, verticals, and regions. Every launch gets adoption targets and a 30/60/90-day activation plan, not only awareness goals. You’ll also make sure what we’re building is communicated publicly, online and through partners. You’ll adapt messaging to regional regulatory and market conditions, and work with product, finance, risk, and support so that each launch is commercially and operationally ready before it goes out. Equip sales, partnerships, and support: You’ll create the sales playbooks, pitch decks, battlecards, case studies, ROI calculators, and objection-handling guides that sales and partnership teams use, and equip support to explain the products as well. You’ll train teams to sell for activation, not just signature. You’ll run win/loss and churn analysis and feed what you learn back into positioning and the product. Represent the market inside the company: You’ll track competitors, pricing, interchange, and regulatory developments, and be the voice of the market and of adoption data in product planning. When acquisitions or product consolidations happen, you’ll support portfolio and integration messaging. What you’ll bring At least 3 years of experience in product marketing at a B2B software, fintech, or payments company. A track record of running launches and measuring them on adoption or usage, not only on awareness. Experience marketing to two audiences at once, such as partners and their customers, or platforms and their users. Working knowledge of how card payments work, or the ability to learn it quickly and explain it accurately. Comfort with data. You can define a metric, build or spec a dashboard, and draw a conclusion from it. Strong writing. You can turn a technical capability into a clear business case for a software company or a small-business owner. Experience building sales enablement that teams actually used. You can take a loosely defined goal, set your own plan, and finish it. You use AI tools every day for research, drafting, and analysis, and you check what they produce. Useful experience Embedded payments, PayFac, or ISV channel experience. Lifecycle or onboarding marketing in a partner-led business. Marketing in healthcare, legal, hospitality, or professional services software. Launching products in Europe or APAC. Running win/loss or churn analysis programs. Hands-on experience with SQL, a BI tool, or marketing automation. Portfolio or integration messaging after an acquisition. Who will enjoy this role You notice when a partner has been live for two months and only a handful of their merchants have enrolled, and you want to know why. Is it the pitch, the onboarding, the partner’s own sales team, or the product? In the same week you might rebuild a merchant onboarding email sequence, pull cohort data for the CEO, train a partnership team on a new vertical, and rewrite a battlecard after a lost deal to a horizontal processor. The scope is wide for one person, and adoption is a harder target than launch coverage. You’ll be judged on numbers you influence but don’t fully control, which means working through partners, product, and sales to move them. Priorities will shift with the roadmap and with acquisitions. Why this role matters ValPay is building products and features for software partners across several verticals and regions. That work has limited impact unless partners and merchants know about it, understand it, and use it. You’ll work directly with the CEO to decide how our products are positioned and how each launch turns into transactions. Your work affects how quickly partners go live, how many of their merchants enroll, and how much volume flows through the platform. You’ll have the authority to set the story and change it when the adoption data says so. _______________________________________________________________________________________ ValPay conçoit des solutions de paiement intégrées pour les entreprises de logiciels. Notre modèle PayFac-as-a-Service permet aux éditeurs de logiciels (ISV) d’offrir des paiements à leurs commerçants sous leur propre marque, pendant que nous prenons en charge la souscription, la conformité et la gestion des risques. Nos partenaires servent les secteurs de la santé, du droit, de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration, des services professionnels et d’autres marchés verticaux. Lancer un produit de paiement, c’est la partie facile. La valeur se crée lorsque les ISV partenaires sont mis en service, que leurs commerçants adhèrent et que les transactions circulent. Nous recherchons une personne responsable du marketing produit dont le succès se mesure à l’adoption : la rapidité et la profondeur avec lesquelles les partenaires et les commerçants utilisent nos produits. Vous serez responsable du positionnement, des lancements et du marketing du cycle de vie dans l’ensemble de nos marchés verticaux, en Amérique du Nord, en Europe et en Asie-Pacifique. Vous relèverez du chef de la direction et travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes produit, ventes, partenariats, canal ISV et opérations. L’IA devrait faire partie de votre façon de travailler. Utilisez-la pour faire de la recherche, rédiger, analyser et automatiser. Vous êtes responsable de la qualité du résultat. Ce qui compte pour nous Un bon jugement et le souci du détail. Mesurer le succès à ce que font les clients, et non à ce que nous avons livré. Prendre ses responsabilités et mener le travail à terme sans qu’on ait à faire de relances. Comprendre comment l’entreprise génère des revenus et se soucier des résultats. L’honnêteté de dire quand quelque chose ne fonctionne pas, y compris dans son propre travail. Ce que vous ferez Stimuler l’adoption par les partenaires et les commerçants : Vous serez responsable de tout le parcours d’adoption : signature, intégration technique, mise en service, première transaction, adhésion des commerçants et expansion. L’écart le plus difficile à combler se situe entre « intégré » et « en transaction active », et c’est vous qui déterminerez où les partenaires et les commerçants stagnent et qui concevrez des programmes pour combler cet écart. Cela comprend des campagnes de cycle de vie, du contenu d’accueil et d’intégration (onboarding) et des guides d’activation pour deux publics à la fois : l’ISV partenaire et les commerçants qui utilisent son logiciel. Avec l’équipe du canal ISV, vous mènerez des campagnes de comarketing et d’adhésion des commerçants qui augmentent le taux de pénétration au sein de la clientèle de chaque partenaire. Mesurer l’adoption et agir en conséquence : Vous créerez et tiendrez à jour le tableau de bord de l’adoption : taux d’activation, délai avant la première transaction, taux de rattachement et de pénétration, volume par commerçant, adoption des fonctionnalités et rétention par cohorte. Vous utiliserez ces données pour segmenter les partenaires et les commerçants, repérer les comptes à risque et faire ressortir les occasions d’expansion, puis vous transmettrez vos constats aux équipes qui peuvent agir. Définir le positionnement et les messages : Vous élaborerez le positionnement, les propositions de valeur et les messages pour chaque produit et chaque marché vertical, ainsi que pour les nouveaux marchés à mesure que nous y entrons. Un volet central de ce travail consiste à expliquer clairement en quoi notre offre de paiements intégrés se distingue des PayFac horizontaux, des processeurs de paiement et des ISO. Vous traduirez les capacités techniques en résultats qui comptent pour les ISV et les commerçants : partage des revenus, fidélisation, rapprochement simplifié et intégration plus rapide. Mener des lancements axés sur l’activation : Vous dirigerez les plans de lancement des nouveaux produits, fonctionnalités, marchés verticaux et régions. Chaque lancement comporte des cibles d’adoption et un plan d’activation sur 30, 60 et 90 jours, et pas seulement des objectifs de notoriété. Vous veillerez aussi à ce que ce que nous construisons soit communiqué publiquement, en ligne et par l’intermédiaire des partenaires. Vous adapterez les messages aux conditions réglementaires et commerciales de chaque région, et travaillerez avec les équipes produit, finances, risques et soutien pour que chaque lancement soit prêt sur les plans commercial et opérationnel avant sa sortie. Outiller les équipes des ventes, des partenariats et du soutien : Vous créerez les guides de vente, présentations, fiches concurrentielles, études de cas, calculateurs de RCI et guides de réponse aux objections qu’utilisent les équipes des ventes et des partenariats, et vous outillerez également l’équipe du soutien pour qu’elle puisse expliquer les produits. Vous formerez les équipes à vendre en visant l’activation, et pas seulement la signature. Vous mènerez des analyses des gains et des pertes ainsi que de l’attrition, et réinjecterez vos apprentissages dans le positionnement et le produit. Représenter le marché au sein de l’entreprise : Vous suivrez les concurrents, les prix, les frais d’interchange et l’évolution de la réglementation, et serez la voix du marché et des données d’adoption dans la planification des produits. Lors d’acquisitions ou de regroupements de produits, vous soutiendrez les messages liés au portefeuille et à l’intégration. Ce que vous apporterez Au moins trois ans d’expérience en marketing produit dans une entreprise de logiciels B2B, de technologie financière ou de paiements. Une expérience concrète de lancements dont le succès a été mesuré par l’adoption ou l’utilisation, et pas seulement par la notoriété. De l’expérience à faire du marketing auprès de deux publics à la fois, par exemple des partenaires et leurs clients, ou des plateformes et leurs utilisateurs. Une connaissance pratique du fonctionnement des paiements par carte, ou la capacité de l’acquérir rapidement et de l’expliquer avec justesse. De l’aisance avec les données. Vous savez définir un indicateur, concevoir ou spécifier un tableau de bord et en tirer une conclusion. D’excellentes aptitudes en rédaction. Vous savez transformer une capacité technique en argumentaire d’affaires clair pour une entreprise de logiciels ou le propriétaire d’une petite entreprise. De l’expérience dans la création d’outils d’habilitation des ventes que les équipes ont réellement utilisés. Vous savez prendre un objectif vaguement défini, établir votre propre plan et le mener à terme. Vous utilisez des outils d’IA tous les jours pour la recherche, la rédaction et l’analyse, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent. Atouts Expérience en paiements intégrés, avec des PayFac ou dans un canal ISV. Marketing du cycle de vie ou de l’accueil et de l’intégration des clients dans une entreprise axée sur les partenaires. Marketing de logiciels dans les secteurs de la santé, du droit, de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration ou des services professionnels. Lancement de produits en Europe ou en Asie-Pacifique. Mise en place de programmes d’analyse des gains et des pertes ou de l’attrition. Expérience pratique de SQL, d’un outil de veille d’affaires (BI) ou d’automatisation du marketing. Messages liés au portefeuille ou à l’intégration à la suite d’une acquisition. Ce poste vous plaira si… Vous remarquez qu’un partenaire est en service depuis deux mois et que seule une poignée de ses commerçants ont adhéré, et vous voulez comprendre pourquoi. Est-ce l’argumentaire, l’accueil et l’intégration, l’équipe de vente du partenaire ou le produit? Au cours d’une même semaine, vous pourriez refaire une séquence de courriels d’accueil pour les commerçants, extraire des données de cohortes pour le chef de la direction, former une équipe de partenariats sur un nouveau marché vertical et réécrire une fiche concurrentielle après avoir perdu un contrat au profit d’un processeur horizontal. La portée du poste est vaste pour une seule personne, et l’adoption est une cible plus difficile à atteindre que la visibilité d’un lancement. Vous serez évalué(e) sur des résultats que vous influencez sans les contrôler entièrement, ce qui veut dire que vous devrez passer par les partenaires, l’équipe produit et les ventes pour les faire bouger. Les priorités évolueront au gré de la feuille de route et des acquisitions. Pourquoi ce poste est important ValPay développe des produits et des fonctionnalités pour des partenaires logiciels dans plusieurs marchés verticaux et régions. Ce travail a peu d’impact si les partenaires et les commerçants ne le connaissent pas, ne le comprennent pas et ne l’utilisent pas. Vous travaillerez directement avec le chef de la direction pour décider du positionnement de nos produits et de la façon dont chaque lancement se traduit en transactions. Votre travail influence la rapidité avec laquelle les partenaires sont mis en service, le nombre de leurs commerçants qui adhèrent et le volume qui circule sur la plateforme. Vous aurez l’autorité nécessaire pour définir le discours et le modifier lorsque les données d’adoption l’indiquent.

jobs.title: Source Inspector - Metal Fabrication & Assemblies
jobs.description: We are seeking an experienced Source Inspector to inspect manufactured components and assemblies before shipment to a U.S.-based industrial fabrication company. Working onsite in Monclova, you will verify that products meet engineering drawings, specifications, approved revisions, and quality requirements. You will identify defects, document inspection results, and help prevent nonconforming products from reaching downstream production. The scope includes fabricated metal components, welded structures, frames, panels, enclosures, sheet-metal parts, machined components, and mechanical or electrical assemblies. This is a practical inspection position working closely with Supplier Quality Management, Supplier Quality Engineering, and manufacturing teams. The role is based in an industrial manufacturing environment involving fabrication, welding, machining, and assembly. Activities include standing and walking for extended periods, using measuring tools, and following required personal protective equipment and site safety procedures. Candidates based in Monclova or surrounding areas are encouraged to apply. Candidates from other locations must be willing and able to work onsite in Monclova. Apply with your updated resume highlighting your fabrication inspection experience, measuring instruments used, and availability to work in Monclova. Responsibilities Perform in-process, final, and pre-shipment inspections of fabricated products and assemblies. Verify product identification, quantities, purchase order requirements, drawing revisions, and applicable specifications before inspection. Inspect dimensions, workmanship, weld appearance, surface finishes, and assembly quality against approved requirements. Perform basic functional checks when specified in the inspection plan. Use calibrated measuring equipment, including calipers, micrometers, height gauges, pin gauges, indicators, tape measures, and squares. Confirm that engineering changes and approved revisions have been correctly implemented. Review material certificates, supplier inspection records, test results, and traceability documentation. Identify and document nonconforming products through clear descriptions, measurements, photographs, and references to requirements. Initiate or support Nonconformance Reports (NCRs) and promptly escalate issues affecting quality, fit, function, or shipment timing. Support containment, sorting, reinspection, and verification of supplier corrections. Withhold product release when requirements are not met or supporting evidence is incomplete, following established procedures and delegated authority. Prepare complete inspection reports and submit supporting documentation within 24 hours of inspection completion. Maintain accurate, traceable records in the designated quality or ERP system. Follow ISO 9001-based quality procedures, document-control requirements, and site safety rules. Requirements At least 3 years of experience in manufacturing quality, source inspection, receiving inspection, fabrication inspection, or supplier quality. Demonstrated experience inspecting fabricated metal products or assemblies in a manufacturing environment. Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, bills of material, specifications, tolerances, and inspection instructions. Working knowledge of GD&T , including its application to drawings using ASME Y14.5. Practical experience using precision measuring and inspection equipment. Working knowledge of ISO 9001 principles , document control, traceability, and control of nonconforming products. Experience documenting quality issues, preparing NCRs, and supporting corrective actions. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Outlook, and the ability to learn ERP and quality-management systems. Strong attention to detail, sound judgment, and clear written and verbal communication. Ability to work independently while coordinating with suppliers, engineering, and production teams. Availability to work onsite in Monclova, Coahuila . Preferred Qualifications Experience inspecting weldments, structural frames, sheet metal, electrical enclosures, busbar assemblies, or mechanical and electromechanical assemblies. Familiarity with weld inspection, surface finishes, coatings, and assembly verification. ISO 9001 internal-auditor training or equivalent quality-system experience. Experience with first-article inspection, sampling plans, and supplier inspection activities. Familiarity with 8D, root cause analysis, 5 Why, and basic statistical process control. Benefits Opportunity to work with an established U.S.-based industrial fabrication company. Exposure to diverse metal fabrication and electromechanical assembly projects. Close collaboration with engineering, manufacturing, and supplier quality teams. Opportunity to strengthen your technical inspection and quality-control expertise. A meaningful role in ensuring product quality and supporting successful project delivery.

jobs.title: Marketing Operations Specialist
jobs.description: Role Summary This role runs the full outbound operation for a go-to-market team, from building prospect lists to handing qualified leads to sales. The person in this seat owns campaign setup and execution across email and LinkedIn, CRM data integrity, email infrastructure and account health, lead reply management, and weekly reporting. This is a hands-on, builder-style role suited for someone who thrives in a fast-moving, early-stage environment where processes are still being built. The role reports to the Head of GTM and Revenue Strategy, who sets strategy, while this person owns execution, troubleshooting, and day-to-day operation of the outbound engine. Key Responsibilities Monitor and manage replies across all outbound channels daily; classify by intent and route next steps Respond to warm leads using approved templates and book demos; hand qualified leads to sales with full context Run follow-up/re-engagement on stalled leads and process opt-outs promptly Keep CRM accurate and current: import/update contacts, companies, activities, notes, stages, deals, ownership Build and maintain CRM workflows, automations, and integrations with outbound tools; run data hygiene Build, launch, and manage multi-step email and LinkedIn campaigns end to end, including sequences, schedules, sending limits, and sender assignment Set up and run nurture and re-engagement flows; apply deliverability best practices; coordinate lists/senders to avoid overlap Pause, fix, and relaunch campaigns based on performance and health checks QA all sequences, templates, and replies against approved copy before launch (personalization, links, subject lines, signatures, compliance footers) Maintain consistent sender identities across mailboxes and LinkedIn profiles; spot-check live sends Manage sending domains, mailboxes, DNS authentication, and warm-up; monitor bounces, spam complaints, blocklists, inbox placement, and domain reputation Scale sending volume based on account health; keep LinkedIn sender accounts healthy and within platform limits; work with vendors to resolve issues Build targeted prospect lists using scraping, hiring-signal, and data tools; deduplicate, clean, and apply suppression Enrich contacts with verified emails/phone numbers across multiple sources; prepare calling lists for sales; manage data credits Deliver weekly performance reporting by channel and funnel stage; build/maintain CRM dashboards; distinguish genuine engagement from automated responses Maintain a live tracker of all running campaigns Administer accounts, seats, subscriptions, and credits across the GTM tool stack Document recurring processes as SOPs; keep naming conventions consistent; support sales with clean data, lead context, and CRM fixes Qualifications 5+ years in marketing operations supporting a B2B outbound or demand generation team Proven experience running multi-channel outbound across email and LinkedIn Strong CRM administration skills Experience managing lead replies and handoffs to sales Working knowledge of email deliverability: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, warm-up, bounce management Experience with list building and data enrichment Advanced spreadsheet skills Sharp attention to detail and clear written English Background in US healthcare or staffing outbound (preferred) Awareness of CAN-SPAM and TCPA basics for US outreach (preferred) Requirements Internet Connection: Primary internet connection with a minimum speed of 15 Mbps . Backup internet connection with at least 10 Mbps . Backup connection must be capable of supporting work during a power outage. Primary Device: Desktop or laptop equipped with at least: Intel Core i5 (8th generation or newer) , Intel Core i3 (10th generation or newer) , AMD Ryzen 5 , or an equivalent processor. A minimum of 8 GB RAM . Backup Device: Must meet or exceed the performance of an Intel Core i3 processor. Must be functional during power interruptions. Peripherals and Workspace: A functioning webcam . A noise-canceling USB headset . A quiet, dedicated home office space . A smartphone for communication and verification purposes. Benefits Join Our Dynamic Team: Experience our fun, inclusive, innovative culture that values your unique contributions and supports your professional growth. jobs.title: Media Buyer / Creative Strategist (Remote)
jobs.description: Media buying is now the easy part. In 2026, the buying itself is piping. The levers that actually move a DTC account are creative, offer, and conversion rate, and the platform keeps getting better at rewarding whoever gets those right. So we don't hire media buyers. We hire marketers who buy media. At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands across our service lines, 20 to 25 of them on paid media, and we spend $6-9M a month on Meta. We're hiring one person to own a handful of those accounts end to end. Here's what "end to end" actually means here. You are the account manager. We don't have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership and accountability: when you're the person answering for the account, it's your result, not somebody else's summary of your result. You are the creative strategist. You do the research, you find the angles, and you write the briefs and the scripts. You direct our editors and designers rather than filing requests with them. Creative isn't a ticket you submit. It's your job. You build the things the account needs. If conversion rate is the bottleneck, you build the landing page. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme. You carry up to six accounts. That's the capacity we run at today, and the team averages about four and a half. You'll manage far fewer accounts than you would at most agencies. In exchange you get real ownership of the results and you get to work as an end to end marketer instead of one station on an assembly line. You can live anywhere. We're a remote team and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you're the client's point of contact and there's nobody else to cover it. The rest of your day is yours. If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we'll both know it fast. If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading. Requirements What the job looks like Own 4 to 6 DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, the creative lead, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $30k/mo to $1M/mo. Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you're the one who answers when something isn't working. Run the research before the ads. Marketing is 80% research here. You mine customer reviews, ad comments, support tickets, and Reddit for the language and objections that become angles. You pull competitor ad libraries. You run our internal tooling that OCRs and transcribes the ads in your account and ties them to performance, so you know what winning and losing actually look like in this account. Write the briefs and the scripts, and direct the work. Creative direction is yours. You run revision rounds with our editors and designers and you hold the quality bar. Ship creative on a cadence. Roughly 8 to 10 new ad launches a week is where accounts hold, in batches every 1 to 1.5 weeks. Informed volume, not spray and pray. We want better hypotheses, not more randomness. Build and test landing pages. Advertorials, comparison pages, PDPs. Built in Claude Code, deployed to Vercel, tested live on a subdomain before anything gets pushed into the client's theme. Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team. Report on new customer economics. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended ROAS and not last click. You'll be expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. You're a fit if You've done this with real money. Hands-on Meta at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. You're AI-native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude (or equivalent) as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. If you can research, write, and build a converting page from scratch, we can teach you the buying. You can write direct response in English at a native or near-native level. Hooks, scripts, ad copy, advertorial. In the customer's own words, not invented. This is the single biggest source of leverage in the role and the thing we screen hardest for. If writing persuasive English isn't a strength, this isn't the job. You can communicate your ideas. This matters as much as anything else on this list. You'll be in front of clients constantly with nobody in between, so you need to be able to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. You have taste and you know when to hand off. You direct creative, you don't half-build it yourself. AI slop shipped to a client is a habit we break, not a shortcut we accept. You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you. Bonus: you've built or operated your own Shopify store or eComm brand. Several of our team have, and it shows. You're not a fit if "That wasn't my role" is in your vocabulary. It's the fastest way to end an interview here. If creative was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the creative. You want to be told what to do this week. You need a ticketing system to know what matters. Benefits Why This Role Is Exciting This is not a maintenance job. You will be surrounded by people who move fast, care a lot, and take the work seriously. You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale. You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

jobs.title: Google Ads Media Buyer / Growth Strategist (Remote)
jobs.description: Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. That is the whole job. Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business. So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face. At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero. You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end. Here is what "end to end" actually means. You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result. You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme. You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number. You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output. If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast. If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading. Requirements What the job looks like Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month. Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working. Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people. Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing. Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target. Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule. Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery. Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why. Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team. Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt. You are a fit if You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search. You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have. You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list. You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard. You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you. Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too. You are not a fit if "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed. You want to be told what to do this week. You need a ticketing system to know what matters. You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question. Benefits Why this role is exciting This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency. You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale. You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident. You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.
